A Defence Ministry notification conveyed the President's approval for his appointment in the substantive rank of Air Chief Marshal with effect from the afternoon of 31st October, 2026, and a tenure up to 31st December, 2028. Over nearly four decades of service spanning operations, flight testing and command roles, he has been involved in aircraft programmes such as the Tejas LCA. News agency ANI reported that his experience is expected to support the government's focus on Aatmanirbharta, or self-reliance, in defence.
items.title: Ashutosh Dixit Takes Charge as India's New Air Chief Marshal

items.summary: A year after remnants of Category 4 Typhoon Halong devastated the Yup’ik village of Kwigillingok, Alaska, residents remain uncertain when they can return home. About 30 people have returned despite largely unlivable housing and infrastructure damage, while most of the former 361 residents are sheltered in Bethel, Anchorage and nearby communities. The village stays under a ‘no-go-home’ order as recovery stalls amid funding gaps; the state committed $75 million, FEMA has paid out about $62.9 million plus $40.2 million in other assistance, but Bryan Fisher estimates total costs will surpass $400 million. Tribal leaders and residents say federal programs are not designed to fund relocation or rebuild mold-infested homes, leaving the community preparing for its second winter.
items.title: Alaska Village Stuck in Recovery Limbo a Year After Typhoon Halong

items.summary: Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, met Elke Budenbender, wife of visiting German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, over tea in Beijing on October 30, 2026. The meeting marked the final day before Steinmeier's state visit to China concluded on October 31. Both women praised their husbands' cultural exchanges and called for continued people-to-people ties between the two nations. Photos were supplied by China Media Group.
items.title: Chinese and German First Ladies Share Tea in Beijing

items.summary: As Americans grow frustrated with rising utility bills, electricity costs have become a prominent issue in this year's midterms. According to Energy Information Administration data, home electricity prices rose more than 10 per cent since the 2024 election, outpacing other goods. In battleground states like Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania—also hubs for new data centers—bills grew even faster. Nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year. Candidates such as Amy Acton in Ohio have pledged to lower bills or freeze rate increases, while Governor Josh Shapiro pressured PECO Energy Company to withdraw a proposed rate hike. Advocates warn that freezing rates may reduce long-term grid investment; Edison Electric Institute's Drew Maloney called the grid 'America's greatest machine,' which does not operate on the political calendar.
items.title: US Midterms Spotlight Utilities Amid Rising Power Bills and Data Center Deals

items.summary: A Navhind Times article argues that Panjim has suffered from the growth of tourism and casinos, which it calls touristification and casinofication. The author contrasts Panjim with Daman, praising its rejection of casinos and clean heritage areas. Two researchers are cited: Antonio Ojeda defines touristification as territorial transformation through tourist activity, while Lidija Lalicic's 2020 paper links overtourism to resident distress or solastalgia. The writer states that Goa University has never studied the social impact of casinos in Goa and blames local government for ignoring residents' needs.
items.title: Panjim residents cite touristification and casinofication as degrading their city

items.summary: The Communist Party of China (CPC) marked its 105th founding anniversary in Beijing on June 26, 2026. Its fifth plenary session adopted a resolution emphasizing full and rigorous self-governance and combating corruption as a long-term task safeguarding public interests. Zhang Fuhai, deputy secretary of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, cited that since the 18th National Congress in 2012, discipline inspection and supervisory organs filed 8.105 million cases and punished 7.922 million people. He outlined four focus areas, including sectors with concentrated power. Huang Jianfa noted the Party has more than 100 million members and over 5.4 million primary-level organizations. Xie Maosong described three measures: making officials afraid to corrupt, unable to do so, and unwilling.
items.title: CPC Outlines Path for Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance

items.summary: Opposition INDIA bloc leaders held a symbolic mock parliament session at Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in New Delhi, led by former Speaker Meira Kumar. Mallikarjun Kharge moved six charges against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, including deletion of roughly 13 to 14 crore voters and unauthorized Form 6 changes. The ruling party disputed the claims; Sambit Patra asserted 'Form 6 amend nahi hua', citing a Supreme Court judgement.
items.title: Congress Leaders Stage Mock Impeachment of Election Commissioner Over Voter Roll Changes

items.summary: The Congress party staged a symbolic public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, tabling six charges including criminal conspiracy to influence elections and deletion of roughly 13 crore voters via the Special Intensive Revision process. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge argued that voting rights under Article 326 face threat from the 2023 CEC legislation. In response, BJP MP Sambit Patra held a press conference rejecting these claims, asserting over 2.8 crore deceased and one crore duplicate entries were removed while shifted voters may re-enlist via Form 6. Patra stated 'Form 6 amend nahi hua', citing a Supreme Court judgement.
items.title: Congress Stages Symbolic Impeachment of Election Commission Chief Amid Voter Roll Dispute

items.summary: A corroded bronze device recovered from a shipwreck off Antikythera, Greece in 1990 is identified as an astronomical calculator built by the ancient Greeks. A 2006 study published in Nature used high-resolution X-ray tomography and surface imaging to reveal at least 30 bronze gear wheels arranged to calculate celestial cycles and predict solar and lunar eclipses. The device also displayed Olympiad-related calendar information, linking astronomy with cultural events. Researchers note that its maker remains unknown and uncertainties persist about its origins and purpose.
items.title: Ancient Greek Device Built to Predict Eclipses Is Revealed

items.summary: Archaeologists excavating a Roman temple complex at Tabard Square in Southwark, London, uncovered in July 2003 a sealed metal pot holding an ancient cosmetic cream bearing the fingerprints of its last user. The container measured approximately 6 centimetres in diameter and was about 2,000 years old. In 2004, researchers from the University of Bristol published findings in Nature after chemical analysis identified animal fat, starch and tin oxide as principal ingredients, each accounting for roughly 40 per cent or remainder. The team led by Richard Evershed later recreated the cream to study its texture and appearance.
items.title: Roman Face Cream Found With Last User's Fingerprints

items.summary: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan said on Saturday that public administration is at a critical juncture and governance must become faster, citizen-centric, technology-enabled, data-driven and outcome-oriented. Speaking at the Indian Institute of Public Administration's annual general body meeting in Delhi, he stressed good governance should be measured by people's well-being rather than economic growth alone, urged administrators to take ownership of their roles, and called for reorienting administrative systems amid India's rapid transformation toward Viksit Bharat.
items.title: VP Radhakrishnan Urges Faster Citizen-Centric Governance at IIPA Meeting

items.summary: The Sikkim Bhutia Lepcha Apex Committee (SIBLAC) urged the state government in a Saturday press statement to expedite talks facilitating the return of the 17th Gyalwa Karmapa, Ogyen Trinley Dorjee, to Rumtek Monastery. General secretary Sangay Gyatso Bhutia cited the electoral promise and reminded officials that the throne has remained vacant for 45 years since the 16th Karmapa's death on November 5, 1981. SIBLAC argued his October 29 arrival in Bhutan offered a timely opportunity before the visit concludes.
items.title: SIBLAC Presses Sikkim Government on Karmapa's Return to Rumtek

items.summary: Carly Dober, a psychologist in Melbourne, argues that relying on AI is harming cognition through cognitive offloading—bypassing the mental effort needed to build neural connections. She notes documented risks including automation bias, depleted brain chemistry, atrophied skills, and the privacy paradox, where people claim to value privacy yet surrender data for convenience. Dober recommends introducing deliberate friction: waiting about 30 minutes before using AI (s37), manually typing credentials, restricting use to desktop computers, committing to writing drafts by hand, asking humans instead of chatbots, and dedicating screen-free hours daily. She frames these habits as brain 'push-ups' that restore cognitive effort.
items.title: Psychologist Warns Against AI Overreliance and Offers Practical Remedies

items.summary: A Mumbai journalist contrasts two recent Bombay High Court benches over how the law treated different groups. In one case, a two-judge Bench ruled against slum dwellers in a garbage petition, calling them “law-breaking encroachers” and blaming 42 per cent of the city’s population for dirty streets while they occupied just 24 per cent of its space (Swachh Survekshan 2025 report). In another case, a single-judge Bench stayed an investigation into CO2 deaths at a Pune factory after arresting the multinational’s MD and CEO. The author links both to Union Carbide’s handling of Bhopal in December 3, 1984 (3,000 died), arguing Indian lives count for less than foreign investors’ prestige.
items.title: Bombay High Court benches criticized for class-based rulings

items.summary: Dozens of protesters gathered Friday outside Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, opposing the government's suspension of its president, which they call unlawful. Police stepped up security around the building and detained several people after demonstrators breached the court's perimeter fence.
items.title: Police Tighten Security at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal Amid Protests

items.summary: Results of Bihar’s eight teachers’ and graduates’ Legislative Council seats suggest shifting voter loyalties, with the ruling BJP losing two sitting MLC seats to opposition RJD candidates. Both winning RJD candidates are upper-caste: Sanjeev Kumar defeated incumbent Nawal Kishor Yadav in Patna Teachers’, ending decades of BJP dominance there, while Anil Kumar Jha beat Sarvesh Singh in Darbhanga Graduates’. Analysts say the outcome signals growing disenchantment among educated voters and a softening caste divide. The JD(U) retained one seat amid internal rivalry involving Anant Singh, who was later expelled after his bail was cancelled by the Supreme Court on December 1, 2026. One activist noted the BJP had lost Bankipur since 1995 as supporters moved toward RJD and JSP candidates.
items.title: Bihar MLC Results Reveal BJP Losing Upper-Caste Support

items.summary: Democratic Republic of Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi asked Russia's Vladimir Putin to help end a standoff with neighbouring Rwanda, which Kinshasa accuses of backing the M23 armed group. The two leaders spoke at a Russia-Africa summit in December 2024. Tshisekedi said he "absolutely" wanted Russian support for peace talks.
items.title: Tshisekedi asks Putin for help against Rwanda-backed rebels

items.summary: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer, Mario Alberto Morales, was indicted by a Texas grand jury for aggravated assault with a deadly weapon after his vehicle struck Miguel Parra Hernandez during an October 10 pursuit in Houston. Prosecutors say video contradicts the agency's account that the victim ran into traffic; ICE denies intentional contact and calls the charge politically motivated. Parra Hernandez, who has lived in Harris County over 30 years, suffered a broken leg and nerve damage. His family disputes details of the operation, including which man was targeted.
items.title: Texas grand jury indicts ICE agent after car strikes fleeing man

items.summary: The US Department of the Treasury issued licenses allowing Hungary's MOL Group to continue negotiating its purchase of Serbian oil refiner NIS, and permitting NIS to keep operating despite sanctions. Both documents expire on December 11. The moves follow reports that talks with Russia's Gazprom broke down after the ruling Serbian Progressive Party lost power in last week's election. Gazprom holds 56.2% of NIS through two firms; Serbia's government owns 29.9%. The Student List party, which won 53% of votes, plans to raise sanctions and gas supply with Russia once it forms the new government.
items.title: US Treasury Extends Licenses for MOL–NIS Refinery Talks

items.summary: President Donald Trump called a Venezuelan oil agreement the biggest in history, citing 17 fields with roughly 64 billion barrels of reserves. Delivery falls to North American Blue Energy Partners, led by Alejandro Betancourt, formerly tied to PDVSA money-laundering probes. The firm claims it will raise output fourfold to over 1 million bpd from about 224,000 bpd in mid-October, granting the U.S. a 35% stake and rights to buy 20% of output at cost.
items.title: Trump's record Venezuela oil deal faces delivery doubts amid firm's murky past

items.summary: The Trump administration approved Friday a proposed sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, the State Department said. The approval goes to Congress for review after Ukrainian authorities reported dwindling interceptor supplies. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned deliveries may begin only in a few years and urged allies to share stockpiled weapons meanwhile.
items.title: Trump Administration Approves Potential Patriot Missile Sale to Ukraine

items.summary: Presumed attackers targeting actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai sent an audio message threatening anyone who works without their alignment or with Salman Khan. Police have not confirmed the gang's involvement, though investigators link the wave to Lawrence Bishnoi, imprisoned since 2014 and designated a terrorist entity by Canada in September 2025. Experts dispute whether this mirrors the 1990s crime wave; S. Hussain Zaidi called calling it a resurgence an exaggeration, while others see extortion driven by Bollywood's wealth.
items.title: Bollywood stars face underworld-linked attacks tied to Lawrence Bishnoi

items.summary: As midterm elections approached, U.S. farmers and ranchers had grown frustrated with rising costs and canceled programs under the Trump administration. On October 19, the president announced $8 billion in diesel relief for farmers hit by price increases tied to the Iran war; a USDA representative called it part of delivering for producers during the 2026 crop year. A week later, on October 26, another $57 million was released for ranchers to expand meat-processing capacity, plus nearly $500 million in commodity purchases. Iowa Farmers Union president Aaron Lehman said farmers had needed help for months, while National Sustainable Agriculture Coalition's Mike Lavender dismissed the payments as a failing solution amid ongoing farm bankruptcies and an unresolved new farm bill.
items.title: Trump's Late-Election Farm and Ranch Bailouts Draw Mixed Reactions

items.summary: Binance said it is discussing a licensed business pathway with the Securities Commission and Bank Negara Malaysia, according to a spokesperson citing Bloomberg. The exchange seeks to re-enter a market where regulators blocked its website and applications since July 2021. Binance reported this week that a security breach may have cost as much as US$6.3 billion (S$8 billion), prompting lawmaker Lim Guan Eng to request an investigation into possible ringgit transactions on its platform.
items.title: Binance in talks for Malaysia licence after five-year absence

items.summary: Groww has opened direct investing in US stocks and ETFs to all customers, giving access to companies such as NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft and Tesla. The platform offers more than 10,000 US-listed securities and supports fractional shares so investors can buy portions of a share instead of full units. Choosing between individual stocks and funds depends on an investor's risk appetite, horizon and objectives.
items.title: Groww Opens US Stock Investing to All Indian Customers

items.summary: The Congress-led opposition unanimously passed a 'resolution' in a Saturday 'mock Parliament' at Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to remove Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Kharge accused him of centralising control and acting on behalf of PM Modi and Amit Shah, while Rahul Gandhi called it a political weapon. The article notes that real removal requires Supreme Court-judge-style grounds with heavy parliamentary majorities.
items.title: Congress bloc holds mock Parliament resolution against CEC Gyanesh Kumar amid electoral roll row

items.summary: The Indian government permitted exports of agarwood oil and chips through Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport in Guwahati, per a Directorate General of Foreign Trade notification published on October 31, 2026. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the approval responds to Chief Minister Himanta Biswa's request and is a logistical boost for Assam and the Northeast. The exports remain subject to all statutory requirements.
items.title: Government permits agarwood oil and chip exports from Guwahati airport

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi accused opposition forces of trying to create instability by spreading lies and rumours, calling them obstructionists after a decade of electoral defeats. He urged citizens to stand together against what he termed 'Dimagi Naxalism,' the threat posed by such mental unrest. The remarks came during Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations in New Delhi on Saturday.
items.title: Modi Accuses Opposition of Conspiring to Divide Nation

items.summary: A massive fire at Hong Kong's Wang Fuk Court last year claimed 168 lives and exposed serious failures in building safety and government oversight, according to an independent committee report released this week. Residents had repeatedly raised concerns about fire hazards, but complaints were passed between authorities without proper action. The Independent Checking Unit relied on contractor certificates rather than checking risks itself. Findings point to misconduct by contractors and consultants alongside departmental failures. In response, the ICU will be disbanded and replaced by a new Public Housing Building Control Section; the housing secretary has resigned. Chief Executive John Lee's determination to hold those responsible accountable is praised as showing that official failures are not simply swept under the carpet.
items.title: Hong Kong draws lessons from Wang Fuk Court fire

items.summary: A CGTN commentator frames the Communist Party of China's Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee, which closed in Beijing on October 29, around a question posed by Huang Yanpei in July 1945 about whether the Communists could escape dynastic cycles of rise and fall. The plenum adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, citing people's oversight over government and Party self-reform as two answers to avoiding that cycle. Drawing on anti-corruption figures from 2025 — including officials investigated and thousands given disciplinary punishments — the piece links these measures to the mass line and a party of roughly 101 million members organized in millions of grassroots organizations, while noting the problems remain unresolved. The author argues self-reform addresses pressures from markets and private capital without abolishing them, with resonance beyond China for ruling parties facing similar dangers.
items.title: CPC's Fifth Plenum Reaffirms Commitment to Party Self-Reform

items.summary: Hainan, an island province in southern China, has introduced a digital reporting system designed to reduce excessive and repetitive paperwork at the grassroots level. The system allows information to be submitted just once and shared across departments. By streamlining reporting, it aims to ease the administrative burden on local officials and free up more of their time to serve the public.
items.title: Hainan Launches Digital Reporting System for Grassroots Governance

items.summary: Government data show more than 5,000 deaths from an ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Eight of 26 provinces are affected, with over 10,300 confirmed cases and a case fatality rate of 48.6%. Public health officials say the epicentre remains Ituri province, a conflict zone that hampers containment. The World Health Organization says greater access to affected areas is needed to end it.
items.title: Congo's Ebola Outbreak Kills Over 5,000 in Deadliest Ever

items.summary: Profits at some of the UK's best-known charity shops have plummeted amid pressures including online secondhand platforms, prompting claims that a key part of the sector's fundraising model could be under threat. According to unpublished accounts seen by the Financial Times, Oxfam's retail profit fell 23% to £4.9m in the last financial year from £6.4m previously. The British Heart Foundation plans to close 150 stores after losses, while Cancer Research UK and Scope have also closed shops. Despite UK secondhand clothing spending quadrupling to £8.8bn a year per GlobalData, donated clothes are increasingly substandard. Robin Osterley of the Charity Retail Association attributed quality decline to fast fashion but disputed online platforms as an issue, citing budget pressures instead.
items.title: UK Charity Shops Face Profit Decline Amid Secondhand Market Shift

items.summary: The UK government’s upcoming budget briefly mentions a new focus on long-term outcomes, giving it one paragraph in the 166-page document. Preventative spending that pays for itself through future savings will be ringfenced from next year via preventative departmental expenditure limits (PDELs). Officials call it an important reform, but departments await Treasury guidance and uncertainty remains over what qualifies.
items.title: UK budget introduces world-first long-term spending protection

items.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed put his cabinet ministers and senior officials through military training at the Hurso centre, saying armed forces discipline could strengthen leadership. The move is unusual in Ethiopia, where civilian officials rarely undergo such training. Participants included Speaker Muferiat Kamil and Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa. It comes amid fighting in Tigray, Amhara and Oromia, plus tensions with Eritrea.
items.title: Ethiopian Prime Minister Sends Cabinet Ministers Through Military Training

items.summary: Reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa will replace Esteban Ocon at the US-owned Formula One team Haas for this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, the team said on Saturday. A spokesman said the change was not due to illness but gave no further details, and the governing FIA confirmed it. The 32-year-old Japanese Hirakawa takes part in his first practice Friday; the race will be his Formula One debut.
items.title: Hirakawa Replaces Ocon for Haas F1 Debut in Mexico City

items.summary: Residents and officials in Urda, Spain, gathered on Saturday (Oct 31) at the San Juan Bautista church near a high-speed train collision that killed at least 69 people. Investigators are examining one of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century, which happened when a Madrid-to-Seville train struck a stationary train on Wednesday. Archbishop Francisco Cerro of Toledo called it
items.title: Spanish Village Holds Memorial Mass for Train Crash Victims

items.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Saturday it has covered 90 per cent of the amount stolen after a record $6.3 billion hack of its platform, Oct 31 reported. The remaining 10 per cent involves less liquid tokens that may take longer to source. Binance set aside around $6.34 billion internally and partially deployed its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). Co-CEO Richard Teng called the breach a 'complex attack' involving a compromised laptop and malicious software. The exchange remains on track to resume withdrawals Sunday, November 1.
items.title: Binance Covers Most of Record Hack Losses

items.summary: The 57th GST Council meeting on October 8 approved a range of process reforms centered on seller registration, returns and refunds. The decisions will be implemented through administrative processes in phases beginning Sunday, November 1, 2026. Changes include simplified registration for small e-commerce sellers, user-friendly filing interfaces, automatic refund processing and greater flexibility on post-supply discounts while retaining safeguards around credit notes.
items.title: GST Council approves registration reforms effective November 1, 2026

items.summary: An Environmental Defense Fund analysis found that the Trump administration provided support to nearly half of the nation's coal plants, helping them continue operating despite economic and regulatory pressures. The study examined 184 grid-connected operating coal plants and reported that 90 received administrative support through cash handouts, Clean Air Act exemptions from pollution limits, and requirements to stay online past their retirement dates. EDF attributed these measures to tools designed to extend plant lifespans while increasing electricity costs and pollution for Americans. NorthWestern Energy defended its Colstrip plant as state of the art technology, while NRG requested exemptions citing compliance costs. The administration stated it saved more than 100 coal plants this term.
items.title: EDF Report Finds Trump Administration Backed Half of US Coal Plants

items.summary: Spain enters a third day of national mourning after a train collision in Urda, Toledo killed at least 69 people. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez says the country is working tirelessly to identify victims while trust in Spain’s rail network has been further shaken. Authorities report 39 injured remain hospitalized and emergency services collected 31 bags of partial remains; authorities say 67 missing-person reports stay open, including 14 for foreign nationals. The crash occurred on a Madrid–Seville line also hit by a January collision that killed 46 people in Andalusia. Driver union Semaf demands urgent review of the failed LZB protection system and has called fresh strikes at Renfe; opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo blames the government for not updating an obsolete safety system.
items.title: Spanish PM faces pressure after deadly Urda train crash

items.summary: A 66-year-old woman from Sau Mau Ping lost around HK$2.7 million to scammers who claimed her bank account was linked to money laundering, the South China Morning Post reported. She transferred HK$2 million and later HK$700,000 into designated accounts before lodging a police complaint on Saturday. Authorities registered it as deception; no arrests were made.
items.title: Elderly Woman Loses Millions After Fake Bank Investigation Scam in Hong Kong

items.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accused Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov of telling “a lot of lies” about the Ukraine war at G20 talks in Atlanta. British minister Ed Miliband also confronted him, urging Putin to accept Russia will not win. Lavrov dismissed Europe’s stance as an arrogant boycott and called Washington’s approach a lesson.
items.title: Kallas calls Lavrov a liar over Ukraine

items.summary: The Rajasthan government approved an Anti-Corruption Bureau investigation against senior IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal over allegations that he misused his position to favour a resort company, causing financial losses to the state. His wife, IPS officer Prashakha Mathur, was also placed on Awaiting Posting Orders. The inquiry centers on 40 villas and cottages allegedly bought by the couple at resorts in Udaipur and Alwar for around ₹15 lakh each, below market value.
items.title: Rajasthan Approves ACB Probe into IAS Officer Over Villa Deals

items.summary: Turkey nominated former foreign minister and longtime UN ambassador Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu for the next UN secretary-general, per state-media reports. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan backed the submission; he has pushed to reform the Security Council. The role would begin January 1, replacing Antonio Guterres after nearly a decade. Sinirlioglu may face opposition from Greece and Israel as seven other candidates compete.
items.title: Turkey Nominates Former Foreign Minister Sinirlioglu as UN Chief

items.summary: BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra mocked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, calling him a 'mock Prime Minister for life' and dismissing opposition protests as pointless. BJP's Sudhanshu Trivedi cited the World Bank report showing India's extreme poverty rate fell to 2.6 per cent in 2023 from 27.1 per cent in 2011, with an estimated 496 million (49.60 crore) people lifted out of poverty.
items.title: BJP Tells Rahul Gandhi He Is a Mock PM for Life

items.summary: The author, who won the Elinor Ostrom Prize from the Institut Ostrom Catalunya, announced a talk in Barcelona scheduled for Wednesday, November 4 at 18:30 local time. Details were linked online, and they invited readers to attend.
items.title: Prize winner announces Barcelona talk on November 4

items.summary: Residents evacuated from Russia-occupied Oleshky arrived in Ukraine under the most significant truce since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The Kherson region ceasefire, which the White House says US first lady Melania Trump helped broker, began Tuesday at 3am and is expected to continue through Sunday evening. About 2,000 residents remained; one humanitarian convoy could safely evacuate more than 750 people. Families separated for over two years reunited at the border.
items.title: Oleshky Evacuees Reach Ukraine Amid Ceasefire

items.summary: This Past Forward column traces how early electric cars were positioned for women drivers, using a mercury-arc rectifier charger and Fannie Goodnow's 1908 Bailey Victoria Phaeton as examples. At the turn of the century, U.S. carmakers grew from about 50 in 1898 to five times that number by 1901, when production reached 7,000 vehicles; by 1910 it had hit 181,000. Electric cars competed with steam and gasoline models, but were marketed as easy to start and clean-running. General Electric ran ads showing women plugging in their cars. Goodnow's charger now sits at Heritage Museums & Gardens in Sandwich, Mass., while her car is lost. S.R. Bailey & Co., which built the Victoria Phaeton after entering electric vehicles in 1906 amid a collapsing carriage business, produced about 500 to 600 such cars before selling its factory in 1915.
items.title: Early Electric Cars Marketed Toward Women Drivers

items.summary: Congress MP Abhishek Manu Singhvi defended an opposition mock parliament held at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence, where bloc leaders passed an impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul Gandhi led the move, alleging treason and voter deletion, while BJP dismissed it as theatrics.
items.title: Opposition Holds Mock Parliament Over Election Commission Chief; BJP Calls It Theatrics

items.summary: The INDIA bloc is holding a large protest at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, November 1, opposing alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls. Organisers expect up to 10 lakh participants, while Delhi Police estimate around 50,000; the ground holds roughly 45,000-50,000 when empty but about 30,000-40,000 with seating and enclosures. The rally runs between 10 am and 5 pm amid extensive security.
items.title: INDIA bloc stages Delhi rally against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

items.summary: Climate policy experts say the upcoming IPCC session in October may resolve a two-year deadlock over when its seventh assessment report (AR7) should be published. Some countries want all reports ready before 2028 to feed the second Global Stocktake, while India and other developing nations argue that rushing would compromise quality and inclusivity. T. Jayaraman and Tejal Kanitkar, both climate policy experts who served on India's IPCC delegations, were interviewed by Frontline. They say reports should be released between May/June 2028 and late 2029 to allow adequate review time. The pair dispute claims that developing countries seek to withhold the report, calling such allegations baseless. They note other scientific sources will inform GST2 regardless of IPCC timing.
items.title: IPCC Nations Clash Over AR7 Report Timeline

items.summary: Residents of Oleshky, a city in Ukraine's Kherson region under Russian occupation since 2022, crossed into Ukrainian-held territory Saturday after an evacuation operation routed through Belarus during a rare truce. The pause in fighting began Tuesday and is the longest along any part of the front line since Russia invaded in February 2022; it was brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, who announced the ceasefire on October 23 (date-1024-1026) and credited her mediation. AFP met evacuees disembarking buses in northern Chernigiv region, where some embraced family members after months of starvation. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said residents would receive needed assistance and thanked the American side for its role (s13-s14). Around 2,000 residents remained before the operation, down from 24,000 pre-invasion (quantity-3088-3103, quantity-3119-3125), per Kyiv's estimates. The truce is scheduled to end Sunday evening (s29).
items.title: Oleshky Evacuees Reunite With Families After Truce-Brokered Rescue

items.summary: A veterinary and conservation team in West Kalimantan rescued 53 Bornean orangutans between August 1 and October 21, 2026 during joint fire-fighting operations. Komara says rising flames force apes to flee higher, making darting dangerous, while many arrive thin and injured. He adds that burned peatland habitats mean rehabilitated animals cannot be released where they were found.
items.title: Team rescues orangutans amid Kalimantan forest fires

items.summary: The Opposition INDIA bloc staged a symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence, accusing him of conspiring to steal elections by ensuring the intentional deletion of 13 crore voters during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. The mock parliamentary event called for his resignation and demanded revocation of the 2023 appointment Act. It followed nationwide protests triggered by a September 23 Indian Express investigation into objections raised by two Election Commissioners over roll revisions.
items.title: Opposition INDIA bloc stages symbolic impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner

items.summary: Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced on Saturday that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had cleared the north corridor of the bullet train project, which will connect Delhi with Agra, Kanpur, Lucknow, Ayodhya, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Patna and Siliguri before extending to Guwahati. Vaishnaw said passengers could travel from Delhi to Kanpur in 1 hour and 45 minutes, while the Delhi-Agra leg would take 59 minutes. The project is expected to be fully 'Make in India', built using Indian capabilities for its construction work including pillars and girders.
items.title: Modi Clears North Corridor of Bullet Train Project

items.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was open to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade but ruled out financial reparations. Writing in The Guardian ahead of King Charles III's Caribbean tour and Commonwealth summit, Burnham pledged difficult conversations while arguing British people today cannot be held liable for historical wrongs from a different age. Denis O'Brien of The Repair Campaign urged London to give a full apology now.
items.title: Burnham Open to Slavery Apology, Rejects Reparations

items.summary: The Bihar education department issued an order on October 30, 2026, banning T-shirts and jeans for teaching and non-teaching staff across state-run schools. Director Vijay Kumar Pandey directed dignified formal attire during office hours and prohibited dancing, DJ setups, disco and vulgar events inside school premises. The notice cited widespread non-compliance with earlier circulars and compared the rule to dress codes at India’s Supreme Court and Patna high court.
items.title: Bihar Bars Casual Wear and DJ Events at Schools

items.summary: The Georgia Court of Appeals reversed a lower court, ruling on October 29, 2026 that software developer Jeff White never formed an enforceable partnership with RutterKey Solutions LLC owner Bruce Mortimer. White claimed he had been promised 30% of joint venture profits since December 2018 and relied partly on a 2022 letter describing a 70-30 profit split. The appeals court found essential terms remained unresolved, so the agreement was only an agreement to agree. It also dismissed White's claims for unpaid services, noting RKS paid him $171,000 to $252,000 annually from 2019 through 2023 and treated him as a W-2 employee, so intellectual property created in that scope belonged to the company. The court observed that recorded profit-sharing discussions may not create an enforceable partnership when fundamental business terms stay undecided.
items.title: Georgia Court Rejects Developer's Profit-Sharing Partnership Claim

items.summary: The Open Space Institute has purchased a four-acre property for $1.3 million from the Margaret M. Rumsey Trust, located between Buttermilk Falls State Park and Route 13 in Tompkins County. The organisation plans to transfer the land to New York State as an addition to the park. Situated at the foot of the gorge that gave the park its name, the site includes a former bed-and-breakfast built around 1825. OSI says it could support a redesigned gateway, reconfigured parking, improved traffic flow, staff housing, and a new trailhead for nearly 400,000 annual visitors. The property will remain closed to the public while OSI owns it before transfer.
items.title: Open Space Institute buys land near Buttermilk Falls State Park

items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate detained Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan from outside Rampur jail as he came out on bail in an alleged PAN fraud case. The 78-year-old will be produced before a special court in Ghaziabad, where officials seek his remand under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The Allahabad High Court had suspended his sentence and granted bail Thursday.
items.title: ED Detains Azam Khan on Bail in PAN Fraud Case

items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency updated its webpage this week, setting a final expiration date of December 31, 2026 for its online web archive. Gretchen Gehrke of the Environmental Data and Governance Initiative said the archive holds irreplaceable information dating back at least 20 years that would be lost if decommissioned. The agency has considered closing it before; after public backlash in 2023, it delayed retirement to July 2023 and later relabeled the move as a “retiring.” Lauren Harper of the Freedom of Press Foundation warned the closure could erode trust amid low confidence in government. The EPA did not respond to a request for comment.
items.title: EPA Sets December 2026 Deadline to Shut Down Its Web Archive

items.summary: Business continued at Conrad Bengaluru on Saturday as police and technical teams investigated the fatal electrocution of two foreign guests in its swimming pool. A hotel representative said staff focused on supporting victims' families, while an Assistant Commissioner confirmed a joint investigation with BESCOM and BWSSB into the pool's pump, lighting and earthing systems. The incident has drawn criticism over safety compliance at luxury hotels nationwide.
items.title: Conrad Bengaluru Opens for Business Despite Fatal Pool Electrocution Probe

items.summary: Senegal is hosting the opening ceremony of the Youth Olympic Games on Saturday, marking the first time an Olympic event reaches Africa as the continent pursues a larger role in international sport. About 2,700 young athletes aged 14 to 17 will compete through Nov. 13 across Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The games were originally scheduled for 2022 but the coronavirus pandemic delayed them by four years. Athletes will contest 153 medal events across 25 sports, including several debuts such as Baseball5, Wushu and coastal rowing beach sprint. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye is set to declare the games open at 6:30 p. m.
items.title: Senegal Opens Youth Olympic Games in Dakar

items.summary: The second and final day of a G20 foreign ministers' meeting is underway Saturday, 31 October 2026, in the US city of Atlanta. Hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the two-day gathering opened with his remarks instead of a traditional group photo, following indications from several European officials that they would not pose alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov amid tensions over the war in Ukraine.
items.title: G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting Enters Final Day in Atlanta Amid Global Tensions

items.summary: A security researcher named Mark Blah released a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-58882, an Android vulnerability dubbed 'SMS of Death.' The zero-click denial-of-service flaw lets attackers crash phones or disrupt calls—including emergency calls—by sending one crafted text message. Google reportedly patched it in its October 2026 updates for Android 14 through 17, but older Android 12 and 13 devices remain vulnerable.
items.title: Android SMS of Death exploit crashes unpatched phones remotely

items.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed police to immediately apprehend the accused who attacked a Class 10 student with a saw inside her classroom at Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu, Anantapur district. The victim sustained severe injuries and another girl was also hurt. Naidu spoke with officials, medical teams, and the family, assuring assistance while condemning the brutality.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Orders Arrest After Classroom Attack on Student

items.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered his military chiefs to respond to any attack on Iran with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response. The orders suggest Tehran would broaden its targets beyond predominantly military ones, widen the war across the region if the US and Israel launch a new attack, update its Targets Bank of US and Israeli assets, and instruct Hezbollah and Hamas to engage. They come after four oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran does not rule out war but welcomed diplomatic efforts, with Qatar mediating talks that shortened an implementation period from five days to two. Iran's Revolutionary Guard attributed the tanker explosions to unauthorised routes and ignored warnings; Oman evacuated 25 crew members off Musandam Governorate, 1. 6 nautical miles offshore." We do not rule out any possibility regarding the outbreak of war," Araghchi said."
items.title: Iran Orders Unrestrained Response to Any Attack

items.summary: The author argues that India is facing an existential crisis at both personal and collective levels, urging society to conduct a 'life review' of its institutions. He traces the term to existentialist philosophy and links it to recent protests over government corruption, exam-paper leaks, and electoral-roll erasures. The piece cites data: Forbes India reports 284 billionaires with roughly $1 trillion in combined wealth for 2025; a World Bank mid-2025 update found extreme poverty fell below the global average at about 2.6%, aided by welfare schemes; yet a 2025 Review of Agrarian Studies study put population below the poverty line at 26.4%. The author blames 'trickle-down' economic policy and an eroded democracy since 2014, framing calls for change as essential to confronting the crisis.
items.title: India's Author Calls for a National Life Review Amid Existential Crisis

items.summary: The government of Senegal is pursuing an ambitious energy diversification strategy under its Vision 2050 plan, aiming to reduce reliance on expensive heavy fuel oil by transitioning to natural gas and renewable energy. According to government figures, oil-based fuels accounted for approximately 72.5 per cent of national power production in 2024. The country also faces high electricity generation costs estimated between 34 and 38 US cents per kilowatt-hour, while consumers pay roughly 24 cents with the difference covered by subsidies. Recent moves include converting its Bel Air plant to LNG, expanding renewable capacity from about 56 MW in 2014 to approximately 624.8 MW in 2025, and announcing 104 oil and gas blocks for exploration. Energy and Petroleum Minister El Hadji Abdourahmane Diouf made the block announcement in October.
items.title: Senegal Targets Gas and Renewables to Cut Power Costs

items.summary: Meta’s agentic AI tool Muse has drawn attention on recent corporate earnings calls, though executives across roughly 50 companies in sectors including travel, internet providers, food and self-storage largely shrugged off immediate disruption. Some described agent-driven bookings as “insignificant” or “quite low,” while others said they expect to benefit from widespread adoption. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg reported that more than 10 million people in the US and Canada had activated Muse, with over 25 percent using it for shopping. Meanwhile, companies like Chipotle are adjusting their websites after agents struggled with loyalty discounts, and Bank of America cautioned customers about sharing login information with AI assistants.
items.title: Meta’s AI Shopping Tool Faces Skepticism From Businesses

items.summary: Inside Climate News reports that the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection issued a new permit in May allowing companies to reclassify conventional oil and gas wells as mineral brine wells, enabling them to sell radioactive wastewater as a product and spread it on roads. David Hess, a former DEP secretary, called the rule ridiculous on its face. Charlie Palladino said roadspreading does not control dust effectively and can damage pavement. Academic research suggests wastewater controls dust no better than rainwater. Karen Feridun testified that over 3.5 million gallons of wastewater had been dumped between 2018 and 2024. DEP says a brine well permit will not necessarily allow roadspreading, but it is drafting regulations to clarify the process.
items.title: Pennsylvania Opens a New Loophole for Oil and Gas Wastewater Disposal

items.summary: In an interview with Living on Earth, pediatrician Dr. Leonardo Trasande discusses a study published in the journal Nature that found micro- and nanoplastics generate free radicals when exposed to water, challenging the assumption that plastic is chemically inert. Trasande explains that increased inflammation may underlie conditions such as cardiovascular disease, heart attack and stroke. He notes this research further unravels why microplastics were linked to a fourfold increase in those outcomes found earlier by the New England Journal of Medicine. The study focuses on one aspect of plastic’s threat while acknowledging chemicals remain a separate concern. Trasande suggests reducing exposure through glass, stainless steel and cast iron cookware rather than nonstick products. He frames environmental exposures as an emerging third risk factor alongside diet and physical activity. Inside Climate News reports the interview.
items.title: Pediatrician Says New Study Shows Microplastics Are Biologically Active

items.summary: S Naren, Chief Investment Officer of ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, spoke at the ET Wealth Expo in Mumbai about why treating individual stocks like asset classes is riskier than diversifying across asset classes. He used 1990 Sensex composition to illustrate how few companies survive over time and argued that beaten-down stocks may never recover their former value. Naren identified NASDAQ and the US dollar as anti-asset allocation bets, noting the dollar moved from 80 to 157 against the yen, while still supporting a small gold allocation. He cautioned investors about chasing strong Indian midcap and smallcap returns since 2020, stressing that individual company performance does not make an entire segment attractive for asset allocation. As he said: 'Stocks need not mean revert at all.' The article carries a disclaimer that expert views are their own and do not represent the Economic Times' position.
items.title: ICICI Prudential's S Naren Warns Against Treating Stocks as Asset Classes

items.summary: Several mutual fund houses have temporarily halted fresh investments in gold fund-of-funds from mid-October, including new SIPs and switch-ins. Reasons are undisclosed but may relate to rising gold imports and strong inflows. Gold ETFs remain open for purchases without a demat account as an alternative.
items.title: Gold FoF Curbs Prompt Investors to Seek Alternatives

items.summary: Reddit announced it will gradually become a logged-in service, limiting full content access for visitors without accounts in selected markets outside the United States. Co-founder Steve Huffman said the change aims to improve personalization and combat scraping, since most unauthorized data access occurs through logged-out pages. Logged users may opt out of personalized advertising; real-name requirements are not needed.
items.title: Reddit to lock content behind logins to fight scrapers

items.summary: Mumbai head coach Amol Muzumdar says the Indian women's cricket team can dominate world cricket consistently within two years, backed by young talent from age-group programs. India won its first ODI World Cup at home last November but has no major T20I title yet. Speaking at an event organised by the Sports Journalists Association of Mumbai (SJAM), Muzumdar and captain Smriti Mandhana will target that gap in the inaugural six-team ICC T20I Champions Trophy.
items.title: India's Women's Coach Sees Dominance Within Two Years

items.summary: A patient at a municipal hospital in Nalasopara West, Palghar district was allegedly assaulted around midnight by two men who entered the ward and attacked him while he lay on his bed. The victim, Kaleem Khan, had been admitted since October 28 after fever and low platelets. Hospital In-Charge Gaurav Wagh said an argument with his wife preceded it; a video has circulated online.
items.title: Hospital Patient Allegedly Beaten By Wife's Brothers In Nalasopara West

items.summary: A 33-year-old woman, Ekta Bhangde, and her six-year-old son Madhav died after falling from a high-rise housing complex in Pimpri-Chinchwad on Friday evening. Wakad police are investigating; bodies were sent for post-mortem. Police said it is likely suicide, noting CCTV showed the mother taking her son to the 18th floor by elevator and no note found.
items.title: Woman and Son Die in Pune High-Rise Fall

items.summary: A Delhi court issued a fresh bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in an eight-year-old criminal defamation case filed by Vikas Pandey. The Saket court directed the warrant be served at his Gurugram address after learning he had left India and that earlier warrants failed—October 17's was sent to an incorrect Austrian address, while another could not be executed because premises were locked. Proceedings have faced repeated service difficulties since 2019; the next hearing is fixed for November 23.
items.title: Delhi Court Issues Fresh Bailable Warrant Against Dhruv Rathee

items.summary: The U.N. biodiversity conference (COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia, produced roughly $1.8 billion in new nature-finance announcements at the close of its session, including a $500 million commitment from the Netherlands to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility on Oct. 26 and another half-billion-dollar contribution from the Global Environment Facility reported that day. Overall biodiversity spending remains far short of the $200 billion per year target set in the Kunming-Montreal framework, with OECD data suggesting annual finance reached no more than $92 billion by 2025.
items.title: COP17 biodiversity conference delivers finance pledges amid shortfalls on spending and subsidies

items.summary: Raids on online scam centers in Madagascar revealed links to a criminal group that ran similar operations in Cambodia, allegedly defrauding African nationals through human trafficking. The sites conducted romance, cryptocurrency and investment fraud, mostly run by Chinese nationals, 148 of whom have been extradited to China, according to Madagascar's justice ministry. Thirteen compounds were dismantled in August and September with U.S. DOJ cooperation.
items.title: Madagascar Raids Expose Scam Centers Linked to Cambodia Network

items.summary: Two men wearing head torches entered the Fondazione Magnani Rocca museum near Parma on March 22, forcing a window and removing Cezanne, Renoir and Matisse works worth about €9 million ($10 million) within three minutes before handing them to an accomplice. A fourth man discharged a fire extinguisher at the gate when the alarm sounded. Director Stefano Roffi said “Whatever could go wrong, did.” The theft follows recent European museum break-ins.
items.title: European Museums Heighten Security After Parma Art Heist

items.summary: A newly published paper in AEJ: Economic Policy by Carl Hase and Johannes Kasinger shows cannabis retailers in Washington state raised prices following organized retail crime. Matching store-level crime data to transaction records, the authors estimate a 1.7–1.8 percent price increase at victimized stores and nearby competitors, consistent with cost shocks rather than demand shifts. They estimate crime imposes about a 1 percent hidden unit tax, costing roughly $30.7 million in social costs borne by consumers.
items.title: Cannabis retailers raise prices after retail crime, study finds

items.summary: A South African court permitted the March and March movement to hold its planned demonstrations under amended conditions, restricting marches between 9am and 3pm and barring weapons or face coverings. Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia sought to block the events over public-order concerns amid unrest in Durban that police say has spread violence; counsel described it as lawlessness requiring more than 400 officers deployed. March and March defended its constitutional right to protest, distancing itself from any violence.
items.title: South African Court Imposes Conditions on Anti-Migrant Marches

items.summary: Washington Governor Bob Ferguson publicly criticized Microsoft after a political action committee ad campaign attacked the state government. The ad, funded by Washington Needs to Compete—which raised roughly $13.8 million including over $5 million from Microsoft—aired during Seattle Seahawks broadcasts and claimed Olympia is broken. Leaked audio shows Ferguson challenging the message at a business summit, citing PitchBook figures of $3.5 billion in startup funding while urging executives to champion Washington's strengths.
items.title: Washington Governor Criticizes Microsoft Over PAC Ad Campaign

items.summary: Multiple news reports indicate OpenAI has lowered its fundraising goal for a new round, which had earlier been reported at $30 billion with valuations of $1.4 trillion and later $1.25 trillion ahead of a planned IPO. The Financial Times reported Friday that the company now targets $20 billion, possibly lower initially, led by United Arab Emirates investors, while The Wall Street Journal said OpenAI has secured $11 billion so far amid tepid interest from large investors.
items.title: OpenAI reportedly cuts new funding round target

items.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Oct 31 it has covered 90% of assets stolen after a record US$6.3 billion (S$8 billion) hack, per a statement dated that day. The remaining 10% involves less liquid tokens that may take longer to source. Binance set aside around US$6.34 billion in company funds and deployed part of its US$1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users reserve. Co-CEO Richard Teng described the breach as a complex attack involving a compromised laptop, while withdrawals are expected to resume Nov 1.
items.title: Binance Replenishes Most of Assets Lost in Record Hack

items.summary: Thousands of people from different communities, including residents of Manipur's hill and valley regions, took part in a rally organised by the Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI) in Imphal. Protesters marched through the streets raising slogans against recent killings linked to an ongoing ethnic conflict.
items.title: Thousands Rally in Manipur Against Recent Killings and Ethnic Conflict

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said on Saturday that the opposition INDIA bloc's first target is Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of acting as an instrument of PM Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah. Speaking at a symbolic public impeachment in Delhi, he warned those allegedly undermining democratic institutions would be held accountable. Around 250 people attended the event, where Mallikarjun Kharge moved a resolution demanding Gyanesh Kumar's impeachment and court trial for treason. BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra dismissed it as a mockery of Parliament.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Names CEC Gyanesh Kumar as Opposition's First Target

items.summary: US Federal Election Commission data show Elon Musk donated at least $445 million to Republican-aligned political action committees since last year. As midterm elections approach, Musk claims a Democratic victory would end US democracy and create a one-party state, writing on X that 51 Republican senators in 2029 are needed to prevent it. His America PAC has contributed to 43 House and Senate races, funding attack ads he cross-posts to his more than 200 million followers. In Texas alone, the campaign provided more than $33 million toward Ken Paxton's Senate bid, plus a $168 million contribution routed through the Senate Leadership Fund. Democratic candidates like James Talarico respond with small-dollar-funded campaigns and ads accusing Musk of trying to buy elections.
items.title: Musk's Midterm Attack Ads Draw Backlash as Democrats Gain Ground

items.summary: Tens of thousands of demonstrators, some in Halloween costumes, marched across France amid cost-of-living and public-services anger; the interior ministry said about 320,000 took part, down from an estimated 410,000 last weekend. Rallies were largely peaceful but police fired teargas and stun grenades as masked rioters hurled paving stones and incendiary devices in Paris, Lyon, Toulouse and elsewhere.
items.title: Police Clash With Masked Rioters After Peaceful Protests Across France

items.summary: A simple explainer describes a cyberattack on Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, which experts widely believe was carried out by a North Korean military hacking unit known as TraderTraitor. The item states hackers accessed investor accounts at 4:05 p.m. Eastern Thursday and took just over $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrencies in about 20 minutes. TRM Labs policy director Ari Redbord calls it the largest bank robbery in human history, while Binance has frozen about $3 billion. Critics note crypto exchanges face weaker regulation than Wall Street firms, citing FTX's collapse and Sam Bankman-Fried's 25-year sentence as context for renewed sector fears.
items.title: Binance Hack Explained as Largest Cyber Heist Ever

items.summary: The District of Columbia and Virginia sued in federal court on Saturday, joining two other lawsuits that seek to halt construction of a proposed memorial arch for Donald Trump. The administration says work could begin as early as next week; Judge Tanya Chutkan is weighing an order until the original veterans’ suit resolves.
items.title: DC and Virginia sue over Trump memorial arch

items.summary: A navy source said China's first shipborne stealth reconnaissance-strike integrated drone, the GJ-21, recently completed its first takeoff and landing aboard the Sichuan. The vessel is China's first independently built Type 076 amphibious assault ship, launched on December 27, 2024, with a full-load displacement of over 40,000 tonnes. Officials noted this marks another breakthrough in operating fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime platforms.
items.title: China's GJ-21 Drone Completes First Takeoff and Landing on Type 076 Ship

items.summary: A notice from Yale described William Nordhaus as one of the true greats following his death. Several MR readers pointed out the news to the writer.
items.title: William Nordhaus, RIP

items.summary: At a hearing in Panama, the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights heard testimony Oct. 27 from representatives of six countries alleging harm linked to Canadian mining companies’ operations abroad, including four alleged attacks on environmental defenders. Indigenous fish-farmer Marco Manobanda testified that El Domo mine, owned by Silvercorp Metals Inc. and Salazar Resources Ltd., is causing deforestation and water contamination in Ecuador. Witnesses urged the commission to recommend mandatory due diligence legislation for Canada. Latin America has been considered the deadliest region for such defenders since 2012, according to Global Witness.
items.title: Latin American Defenders Testify Against Canadian Mining Ties at OAS Body

items.summary: MotoGP will proceed with the postponed Qatar Grand Prix despite rider demands for stronger safety assurances, organisers arguing a zero-risk environment is unrealistic. The event was moved to November 6-8 due to regional conflict. MotoGP's spokesperson said every available assurance has been provided and safety remains everyone's priority, while championship leader Marc Marquez sought an organisational safety plan rather than declining to attend.
items.title: MotoGP Proceeds With Qatar Race Amid Rider Safety Concerns

items.summary: Binance, described as the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of $6.3bn (£4.7bn) in assets stolen Thursday, calling it crypto's biggest hack on record. The firm set aside more than $6.34bn and vows to absorb losses rather than shift them to users. It aims to reopen withdrawals Sunday 1 November. Two blockchain analytics firms point to North Korea's Lazarus Group; the FBI blames Pyongyang for a separate Bybit theft, which North Korea denies.
items.title: Binance Covers Most Losses After Record Crypto Hack

items.summary: Manchester City suffered their second consecutive Premier League loss, falling 1-0 at home to third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion through an early goal by Yasin Ayari. Enzo Maresca's side took the lead but lost control in the final 30-40 minutes and managed only six shots on target against keeper Bart Verbruggen. City remained top of the table on 21 points, ahead of Arsenal on goal difference. Manchester City midfielder Elliot Anderson said: 'We created a lot of chances, disappointing to lose.' Brighton remain third with 19 points after nine games.
items.title: Manchester City suffer home defeat to Brighton

items.summary: High-street retailers are staging a comeback by courting luxury fashion, A-list collaborations and enhanced services rather than relying solely on trend-led affordable designs. Marks & Spencer showcased a catwalk collection at London Fashion Week with half the pieces under £50; Topshop now has concessions in 30 John Lewis stores. Asos appointed stylist Law Roach as stylist-in-residence after sales fell 12% last August, then reported 50% profit growth this March. M&S says designing for longevity helps wardrobes last longer, while critics note high-street garments are often made from human-made fibres rather than luxury fabrics.
items.title: High-street brands court luxury and AI as they stage a comeback

items.summary: Critics on both sides of politics accused John Healey of dodging major questions in his first budget, arguing he failed to announce reforms that could address Britain’s chronic housing problems. The Resolution Foundation described it as a scatter-gun approach more concerned with politics than economics. Oxford academic John Muellbauer calls the UK system “one of the most dysfunctional in the world,” tracing its affordability crisis to decades of land and housing policy failures. Treasury proposals from Muellbauer aim to remodel council tax into an annual household levy while abolishing stamp duty, though Rachel Reeves kept the banding system rather than applying a percentage above £2m homes. Torsten Bell advocates for fundamental reform, warning that powerful owner-occupier lobbies will resist change before any progress occurs by 10 years from now or two and a half years away at the next election.
items.title: Healey’s Budget Criticised for Failing to Tackle Housing Crisis

items.summary: At an EU-Canada summit in Montreal, Prime Minister Mark Carney and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the 'Alliance for the Future', a partnership covering more than 20 areas of cooperation including critical minerals, defence, technology and resilient supply chains. The move comes amid trade tensions under US President Donald Trump, whose tariff threats have prompted both governments to reassess dependencies. Von der Leyen said relationships once seen as stability guarantees are now used as pressure tools. Carney stressed the alliance is not an anti-American bloc but expands Canada's strategic options. A proposal for Canada to become the EU's first associate member also drew debate over its structure and terminology, which some members questioned.
items.title: Canada and EU Launch Strategic Alliance to Reduce US Dependence

items.summary: The Australian Broadcasting Corporation's ABC presents a Wordage quiz titled 'Let's splash some cash,' in which participants sort words and phrases for money according to how old they are. Players drag each term into shaded boxes, receive three guesses per round across three rounds, and may request hints if stuck. Sources cited include the Oxford English Dictionary, Etymonline, Green's Dictionary of Slang, Merriam-Webster, and Macquarie Dictionary.
items.title: ABC Wordage quiz challenges readers to age money terms

items.summary: The Upstage Theatre Company in Melbourne's south-east says it was caught up in a catfishing scam. A person claiming to represent a church asked them to set aside about 150 tickets for their production of Jesus Christ Superstar, then disappeared before the performance. Co-founder Scott Hili said they were left with more than 150 empty seats and lost $7,500 in ticket sales. He described it as a "kick in the teeth" and said the company may have to close if it cannot fundraise about $8,000 owed for the production. Victoria Police confirmed receiving the report but said no criminal deception offence was met because no financial advantage was obtained.
items.title: Melbourne theatre company considers closure after catfishing scam over ticket sales

items.summary: Markets regulator SEBI barred carbon-credits trading firm EKI Energy Services Ltd and Managing Director Manish Kumar Dabkara from the securities market for two months and 12 months, respectively. In its 94-page order, SEBI said EKI prematurely recognised revenue of Rs 197.04 crore in FY23 and overstated expenses by Rs 26.34 crore across FY22-FY23 to divert funds. The regulator imposed monetary penalties totalling Rs 88 lakh on the company and individuals, directed Dabkara to recoup diverted amounts, and barred other directors for up to eight months. Penalties were payable within 45 days.
items.title: SEBI Bars EKI Energy MD Over Financial Misrepresentation

items.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah married television journalist Nidhi Razdan on Friday, according to news agency PTI. Omar posted on X that “a new journey began yesterday,” while Razdan confirmed it with the remark, “It’s done, bro.” PTI said the marriage was solemnised under the Special Marriage Act and cited sources for details about witnesses and functions held in Srinagar and New Delhi. The union comes three months after a Supreme Court decision granting Omar Abdullah a divorce from Payal Abdullah.
items.title: Jammu and Kashmir CM Omar Abdullah Marries Journalist Nidhi Razdan

items.summary: The Information reported on Saturday that Meta built a prototype humanoid robot with the Chinese startup company Fourier and is developing a second version. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
items.title: Meta Builds Humanoid Robot With Chinese Startup Fourier, The Information Says

items.summary: The U.S. Embassy in Moscow issued a security alert warning of a credible threat to the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve, located at Dolskaya Ulitsa 1, on October 31, 2026. The embassy described it as aware of a possible mass casualty event that day and urged visitors to avoid the site, steer clear of crowded areas, remain alert, review their personal security plans, keep phones charged, carry identification, monitor local media, and enroll in STEP for updates.
items.title: U.S. Embassy Issues Security Alert for Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow

items.summary: Omar Yaghi, a Nobel laureate, describes Atoco's atmospheric water unit as roughly the size of a 6-meter shipping container. The company says it can produce up to 1,000 liters of clean water daily with little power and no grid link. Interest follows repeated Caribbean hurricanes in 2024 and 2025 that left residents without water; Atoco frames air capture as more climate-friendly than desalination brine dumping. The claims come from the company, and the device has not yet been tested in the field.
items.title: Nobel chemist's air-water device draws Caribbean interest

items.summary: The third consecutive weekend of France's social mobilisation drew some 320,000 participants nationally, including 70,000 in Paris, per the Interior Ministry. The figure fell from 410,000 on 24 October to 550,000 on 17 October; organisers claimed 800,000 each day. Tensions rose during dispersals across major cities as transport disruptions and police measures prompted arrests and tear gas use in Lyon.
items.title: France's Third Protest Weekend Sees Lower Turnout and Early Clashes

items.summary: Euronews aired its October 31, 2026 evening news bulletin, presenting a brief roundup of top stories across Europe and beyond. The program covers world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel with contextual framing. Described as reported with independence and a European perspective, the regular round-up offers viewers a clear overview of current events shaping global developments.
items.title: Latest news bulletin | October 31st, 2026 – Evening

items.summary: A Rajasthan Anti-Corruption Bureau probe examines a former Additional Chief Secretary and his IPS wife over 40 villas bought for Rs 6.16 crore at two Ananta resorts, then leased back to the seller, Goyal Fashions Private Limited, reportedly earning Rs 1.8 crore annually. The ACB said its preliminary inquiry found prima facie evidence of collusion with company directors and undue favours in resort construction, approvals and financial packages. Both officers were placed under Awaiting Posting Orders; Agrawal's property return listed 14 properties while Mathur declared none. The investigation covers misuse of position, benefits to the firm and source of funds.
items.title: Rajasthan IAS-IPS Couple Under Corruption Probe Over Resort Villas

items.summary: A scholar at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University asks whether younger consumers now evaluate cars the way they assess smartphones, arguing that electric-vehicle expansion and smartphone makers such as Xiaomi and Huawei are turning vehicles into software platforms. He says millennials and Gen Z prioritise in-car technology, charging infrastructure and ecosystem integration over brand prestige or mechanical engineering, choosing purchases through online channels rather than dealerships. Research he cites shows these buyers weigh data security heavily; one study claims screen-based reaction times while driving can be worse than impairment from alcohol or drugs. The author notes a corporate blind spot: 80% of automotive executives believe they deliver an exceptional digital experience, yet only 8% of customers agree.
items.title: Younger buyers judge cars like smartphones, research argues

items.summary: Crypto exchange Binance said on Saturday it has replenished 90 per cent of the assets stolen in a record $6.3 billion hack, buying new tokens with company money. Co-CEO Richard Teng stated users would not bear the financial impact and withdrawals were still expected to reopen Sunday. Analysts blamed North Korea for the breach, which involved a compromised laptop and software designed to delete evidence.
items.title: Binance Covers Most Losses From Record Hack

items.summary: The NMC Healthcare founder, Dr Bavaguthu Raghuram Shetty, has filed two interim applications with the Bombay High Court on October 29, 2026. He seeks security of USD 15 billion matching his damages claim, disclosure of a USD 600 million settlement paid to NMC's joint administrators in June 2026, and forensic imaging of Bank of Baroda records across Abu Dhabi, Dubai and DIFC branches. Shetty accuses the lender and 25 other defendants of fraud, negligence and collusion; he relinquished control after fraudulent transactions allegedly siphoned funds until around 2019. The allegations remain untested, and the bank has not yet filed its reply.
items.title: NMC Health Founder Seeks Settlement and Security in $15 Billion Suit

items.summary: India won the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship 2026, becoming its first men's champions by beating Sri Lanka 54-20 in the final on Saturday in Ahmedabad. The victory completed a double after India's women beat Uganda 35-15 earlier. Aditya Shinde led with 10 raid points and Bharat Hooda added eight; Pankaj Mohite scored six, while Naveen Kumar contributed five. India finished unbeaten with eight wins from eight matches, topping Group A before defeating Bangladesh in the semifinal.
items.title: India Win First Commonwealth Kabaddi Men's Title and Complete Historic Double

items.summary: Police say a 21-year-old man, Hemanth alias Dummu, attacked a 15-year-old girl at her government school in Anantapur using a chainsaw on Saturday morning. The accused is the victim's maternal uncle and had allegedly harassed her for some time in the name of love before entering the classroom around 10.30 am and severely injuring her face, neck and back. Her family alleges he was harassing her earlier.
items.title: Andhra teen attacked with chainsaw by her uncle in classroom

items.summary: The Delhi Traffic Police issued a traffic advisory for Sunday, November 1, warning commuters of possible disruptions on Jail Road due to a proposed padyatra from Hari Nagar DTC Depot to Tilak Nagar Metro Station. Between 9 am and 3 pm, both carriageways between Lajwanti Chowk and Tilak Nagar may be temporarily closed as diversions are likely.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police Warns of Sunday Padyatra Disruptions on Jail Road

items.summary: The Telugu Desam (TD) lodged a complaint with the State Election Commission alleging voter inducements and electoral irregularities in the Chimakurthy and Nandikur municipalities. TD state general secretary Parchuri Ashok Babu and AP education corporation chairman Kuppam Rajasekhar submitted the representation on Saturday, seeking an inquiry into alleged cash distribution to voters. The complaint claims Rs 2,000 per vote for YSRC's fan symbol supporters, with Rs 8,000 offered for four votes.
items.title: TD Complaint Alleges Cash Voter Inducements in Two Municipalities

items.summary: The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) served show-cause notices to Taj Falaknuma Palace, Golconda Hotel and Resorts, 36 Arabian Kitchen and other establishments after Saturday inspections found serious violations. Inspectors reported pest infestation, expired food, frozen meat stored beyond its shelf life, cooking oil with a total polar compounds count of 27 against the limit of 25, and cockroaches in drinking-water tanks. TG SAFE suspended FSSAI licences of 14 establishments across Golconda and Charminar zones after finding unhygienic kitchens; further action including penalties will follow as proceedings continue.
items.title: Telangana Food Authority Serves Notices and Suspends Licences at Hyderabad Eateries

items.summary: The Rajasthan government placed IPS officer Prashakha Mathur, wife of IAS officer Shikhar Agarwal, on awaiting posting orders amid an Anti-Corruption Bureau inquiry into alleged property purchases at prices below market rates. The couple allegedly bought 10 villas each in March 2026 at ₹15 lakh apiece. A separate ACB investigation examines benefits to the Ananta resort company and transactions tied to a financial package issued on March 27, 2026. HT contacted Agarwal and Mathur but had received no reply.
items.title: Rajasthan Places IPS Officer on APO Amid Villa and Resort Probe

items.summary: Cloud hosting platform Northflank warned customers on October 30 to rotate credentials after a security breach led to unauthorized use of their AI API keys. The company disclosed the incident following an alert from cloud security firm Wiz, instructing users to assume environment variables had been decrypted and secrets stolen. Multiple customers reported unauthorised key usage, prompting advice to review billing logs and report suspicious activity. Northflank has not disclosed how attackers accessed systems or how many customers were affected.
items.title: Northflank Security Breach Leads to Abuse of Customers' AI API Keys

items.summary: Government data on Saturday put Congo’s Ebola deaths above 5,000 at 5,026 out of 10,351 infected, a nearly 50% lethality rate. The Bundibugyo outbreak, declared in mid-May and already the second deadliest in history after West Africa's 2014-2016 toll of 11,000 deaths, has reached 67 of 178 health zones across eight provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu accounting for most cases. Experts cite weak contact tracing: about 80% of new cases come from unmonitored chains, per the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
items.title: Congo's Ebola toll passes 5,000 as spread widens across provinces

items.summary: Heavy rainfall triggered a landslide at Gidipabali village in Ganjam district on Friday, leaving twelve persons missing after thirteen had been relocated from the hamlet of 26 people.
