Separately, three family members including a nine-month-old baby died in Kandhamal district, and another death was reported in flood-related incidents in Gajapati district amid Cyclone Arnab's effects.
items.title: Landslide in Ganjam leaves 12 missing; Cyclone Arnab kills and displaces across Odisha

items.summary: A convoy of heavily armed Salvadoran troops was seen in the Tabarre neighborhood of Port-au-Prince on Friday. They are part of 2,000 troops that El Salvador President Nayib Bukele deployed this week after a gang attack left four aviation technicians missing. Haiti's government says they were abducted. Bukele wrote his country only wants to bring them home and is not seeking to dominate Haiti or seize its wealth.
items.title: Salvadoran Troops Deployed to Haiti Amid Gang Violence Concerns

items.summary: Researchers at University of Michigan Engineering propose E-CALC, a system that tracks energy use across an AI workflow. DARPA will fund the project for two years at $1.83 million with partners UIUC and BAE Systems. Principal investigator Mosharaf Chowdhury says it aims to deliver widespread benefits while minimizing energy use.
items.title: DARPA Funds Project to Track AI Energy Use Across Its Workflow

items.summary: On the latest Weekend Ka Vaar episode of Bigg Boss 20, host Salman Khan recalled standing up for his aide Shera after a female friend made remarks about him. He said he stopped her immediately to show boundaries and used the story to teach housemates about defending themselves and loved ones when lines are crossed.
items.title: Salman Khan Recalls Standing Up For Shera On Bigg Boss 20

items.summary: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi warned the BJP against backing chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, saying he would not survive in his position for long and hinted at a possible revelation. The INDIA bloc unanimously passed a resolution to impeach Kumar on six charges including electoral manipulation and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls ahead of its Ramlila Maidan rally. BJP called it a mockery; spokesperson Sambit Patra dismissed the allegations as lies.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi warns BJP over CEC Kumar

items.summary: Police in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh registered cases after cyber fraudsters cheated a woman of Rs 90,000 by posing as customer care staff while she tried to return an online purchase. An unidentified caller contacted her and sent a link that hacked her phone; messages then showed the transfer. Other victims across Piplani, Aishbagh, Ashoka Garden, Misrod, Bagsewania and Koh-e-Fiza reported losses from Rs 37,000 to Rs 5.89 lakh, with the largest loss of Rs 5.89 lakh suffered by a youth under the Koh-e-Fiza police station.
items.title: Bhopal Police Investigate Online Return-Order Scam

items.summary: During a recent interview with Wired's Steven Levy, Apple CEO John Ternus defended the company's current position in the AI landscape. Over the past couple years, Apple has often been described as behind on AI, especially after delaying a more powerful version of Siri that finally launched this summer. While acknowledging 'everyone has an opinion,' Ternus insisted he liked where they were and said Apple is absolutely going to leverage AI.
items.title: Apple CEO Defends Company's AI Position Amid Criticism of Lagging Progress

items.summary: A federal judge denied xAI’s motion to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of operating at least 35 combustion turbines and other air pollution sources at its Colossus data center outside Memphis without required permits, in violation of the Clean Air Act. Judge Debra M. Brown ruled that plaintiffs have statutory standing under Mississippi’s State Implementation Plan and dismissed xAI’s mobile-source exemption argument. The NAACP called it another victory in holding xAI accountable.
items.title: Federal Judge Lets NAACP Pollution Suit Against xAI Proceed

items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh state disaster response and fire services department will introduce a WhatsApp-based facility on November 1 to issue recommendation reports for temporary firecracker shop permissions. Applicants send details through WhatsApp number 9441236448, pay the prescribed fee of Rs 500 via UPI or QR code, and download their Temporary Firecracker Recommendation Report automatically without visiting offices. The department said the process had been automated to eliminate physical visits and manual intervention by officials. Director-General P. Venkata Ramana urged owners to use the facility from November 1.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh launches WhatsApp firecracker shop recommendations from November 1

items.summary: Snorkel AI, which builds data development tools used by annotators and model providers, describes using Databricks' serverless Postgres database, Lakebase, to give each pull request its own production-like environment. Previously restoring a full copy of its Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster took about 20 minutes per environment, slowing the merge queue. Shared staging databases or synthetic data reintroduced test interference and stale schemas. Snorkel now keeps a golden main branch replicated from Aurora within about 2 minutes via AWS DMS, then creates an isolated branch when a PR opens—ready in under a minute—and deletes it on close using TTL as a backstop. Copy-on-write branching makes branches instant and cheap; each adds only about 5 to 10 GB over the shared base. Snorkel also applies the same pattern to AI agents running SQL, with per-task branches that scale compute to zero when idle.
items.title: Snorkel AI adopts Lakebase branching for CI/CD

items.summary: At a parade marking Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary, PM Narendra Modi said the next major priority is fully securing India's borders. He criticised opposition parties for abandoning their constitutional duty in favour of obstruction driven by despair and disappointment. Modi recalled how Patel and BR Ambedkar defined government and opposition roles while framing the Constitution.
items.title: Modi Blames Opposition for Abandoning Constitutional Duty Amid Border Priority

items.summary: The INDIA bloc passed a symbolic resolution Saturday in New Delhi to 'impeach' Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of colluding with the BJP and compromising election management. Around 250 opposition MPs attended at Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge's residence. Rahul Gandhi said SIR deleted 15% of 2024 voters, calling LS polls illegal. Leaders warned of electoral threats; some drew parallels to Germany in the 1930s.
items.title: Opposition MPs Symbolically Impeach Election Commission Chief

items.summary: Hundreds of thousands protested across France ahead of an upcoming general strike, driven by rising living costs and poor public services. Police fired tear gas in Paris during a third weekend of demonstrations. Around 320,000 people took to the streets nationwide, with at least 290 arrested per France's interior ministry, while police estimate about 70,000 gathered in Paris alone. Protests also occurred in Albania, Germany and Italy. BBC correspondent James Waterhouse reported on the youth-led movement across Europe. Authorities prepared heavily to prevent a repeat of earlier violence.
items.title: Protests Spread Across Europe as France Prepares for General Strike

items.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is hosting the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, focusing on economic and security challenges. The item's opening line characterizes his effort as difficult: he has a tough time getting officials at the G20 on the same page. No figures or dates appear in this short piece.
items.title: Rubio Struggles to Align G20 Officials in Atlanta

items.summary: A new local government has taken its seat in the southern Philippines, described as a milestone in the peace process for a conflict that has lasted some 80 years. The statement frames this development within an ongoing effort to end decades of fighting in the region.
items.title: New Local Government Marks Milestone in Southern Philippines Peace Process

items.summary: A man, aged 35 per the report, has been charged under the Explosives Act and Firearms Order after police searched properties across north Belfast on Friday and Saturday. He faces two counts of possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances plus possession of a prohibited weapon. Searches at Shankill Road and Edwina Street areas located devices seized for forensic examination as part of an evacuation operation; residents have since been allowed home. DCI McCallum said inquiries continue, with the public urged to contact police on 101 quoting reference number 261 30/10/26.
items.title: Man Charged Over Explosives and Firearms Seizure in Belfast

items.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Saturday it used company money to replenish about 90% of the roughly US$6.3 billion stolen in a large hacking attack, pledging full coverage of losses while user withdrawals stay on track to resume Sunday; the remaining 10% are less liquid tokens that may take longer to source. Investigators point to hackers linked to North Korea as responsible for what Binance called a complex attack with several points of breach.
items.title: Binance Covers Most of Hack Losses With Company Funds

items.summary: Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner said he could become the fifth or sixth manager dismissed in little over a year unless results improve, following a 2-0 defeat at Brentford that left them bottom three with one win from nine games. He told a press conference on Oct 31 that change was needed and promised to make it without compromises.
items.title: Glasner Warns of Sacking if Forest Fail to Turn Season Around

items.summary: Hundreds of residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied front-line city of Oleshky, crossing into northern Ukraine via Belarus on Saturday. Olha described years there as 'Horror', while her husband Viacheslav said they had come back from hell after fearing mined escape routes. A humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump enabled evacuation; up to 6,000 people were believed still in the area, with 1,700 in the city itself.
items.title: Ukrainians describe horror of life in Russian-occupied Oleshky before evacuation

items.summary: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky were reunited with family members after crossing into Ukrainian-held territory on Saturday, following a major rescue operation that began Friday under the most significant truce since Russia’s full-scale invasion four and a half years ago. Volunteers, Red Cross workers and aid groups welcomed them at the border. Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets called it an important moment for those finally safe. An estimated 2,000 people remained in Oleshky when the truce took hold. Separately, Russia’s defence ministry said its forces shot down 433 Ukrainian drones overnight, and Ukraine reported drone attacks left 280,000 households without power.
items.title: Oleshky Evacuees Reunite With Families After Truce Crossing

items.summary: Anthony Albanese’s Grayndler electorate is pushing back as Labor considers letting AI companies scrape Australian creative works by default to train models. The seat hosts more than 3,000 cultural and creative businesses, with 10% of its workers in those fields versus 4.2% nationally. Screenprinter Pete Strong called the move an “extraction industry mining for profit,” while author H Morgan-Harris warned the ecosystem could be decimated; designer Lu Campbell-Smith said opting out was outrageous. The draft laws are expected by year-end, with parliamentary consideration due in 2027. Labor’s proposals were leaked after OpenAI met ministers over training models locally. Albanese promised strong protection but disapproval stands at 56%, the equal highest since he took office.
items.title: Grayndler creatives unite against federal AI copyright proposal

items.summary: Alex de Minaur defeated Alexander Zverev, the new world number one, in three sets at the Austrian Open semi-final. He won 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 (4), including a deciding tiebreak with 25 winners total. The victory qualifies him for the ATP Finals in Turin and sets up a final against Carlos Alcaraz.
items.title: De Minaur beats Zverev to reach Vienna Open final against Alcaraz

items.summary: Australian eating-disorder specialists are warning that the booming global wellness economy is harming young people's body image and encouraging disordered eating. Kathleen McBride, a recovered bulimia patient now working in recovery on Queensland's Sunshine Coast, says traditional dieting messages have been repackaged as 'wellness' through social media algorithms. The Butterfly Foundation warned of this influence; its data states eating disorders affect more than 1.1 million people across Australia, with the number increasing by more than 21 per cent since 2012. An international study found anorexia and bulimia affected about 18.1 million people worldwide in 2023, up 71 per cent since 1990. Experts call for better duty-of-care laws to regulate harmful content.
items.title: Eating disorder experts warn against online wellness trends

items.summary: Tens of thousands of young people protested across Germany Saturday, organised by the collective GenZ regelt!, demanding more education funding and protesting the high cost of living. Police clashed with masked demonstrators using water cannon and pepper spray after protesters hurled stones, fireworks and bottles; several officers were injured. The movement rejected violence and said 120,000 people took part.
items.title: Gen Z Protests in Germany Demand More Education Funding

items.summary: Aleksandar Vucic lost Serbia's October 25 election to the Student List, which won 53% of the vote against his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) at 39%. The party emerged from a student revolt triggered by the collapse two years ago of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad that killed sixteen people. Since winning, critics have removed Vucic portraits and lodged complaints about Informer TV; journalists' associations now call for its license revoked. Analysts say society expects justice amid an unresolved power vacuum while SNS retains influence. The Student List prioritizes domestic reform and EU accession without changing foreign policy or Russia sanctions. A repeat vote is scheduled for November 1 at around fifty stations due to irregularities before parliament convenes.
items.title: Serbia's Student List Wins Election; Vucic Faces Fallout

items.summary: A CGTN commentary argues that the October 30, 2026 meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Beijing carries significance beyond bilateral diplomacy. The author contends differences need not define relations, citing mutual respect and economic complementarity as foundations for cooperation. China-Germany ties are framed as central to Europe-China economics, with automotive firms like Volkswagen and BMW illustrating deepening interdependence rather than simple export destinations. Emerging sectors including AI-enabled manufacturing and green hydrogen offer future growth areas. The piece notes the partnership approaches its 55th diplomatic anniversary in 2027.
items.title: Xi-Steinmeier Talks Signal Deeper China-Germany Economic Partnership

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta focused on strengthening global energy security, securing critical mineral supplies, and addressing vulnerabilities in international supply chains amid growing geopolitical tensions. Speaking at the conclusion of the gathering, he emphasized returning the forum to its economic mission while noting countries agree a problem exists but work remains to reach collective solutions.
items.title: Rubio Says G20 Meeting Focused on Energy, Minerals and Supply Chains

items.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk delivered a televised address Saturday evening amid escalating tensions over the Constitutional Tribunal, accusing PiS and President Karol Nawrocki of undermining judicial independence. The dispute dates to 2015 when Civic Platform and opposition parties clashed over five judges. Tusk described Friday’s events as “scandalous incidents,” pledged security for newly elected judges, and warned against pro-Russian exploitation, though the speech offered no concrete agreement with Nawrocki.
items.title: Tusk Vows No Compromise on Rule of Law After Tribunal Clash

items.summary: The Abu Dhabi Grand Slam ended its final day with heavyweight judo finals. Ivaylo Ivanov of Bulgaria won his second grand slam title in 11 years, while Yelyzaveta Lytvynenko of the UAE took gold on her first world championship appearance. Idar Bifov defeated France's Aurelien Diesse at -100kg, Helena Vukovic beat Israel's Raz Hershko at +78kg, and Georgia's Irakli Demetrashvili won his second grand slam gold of the year over Azerbaijan's Ushangi Kokauri. Judo legend Teddy Riner attended the event.
items.title: Abu Dhabi Grand Slam Judo Finale Delivers Heavyweight Golds

items.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Türkiye nominated Ambassador Feridun Sinirlioglu as a diplomatic contribution meant to overcome an impasse in the UN secretary-general selection process. Ankara formally submitted the nomination on Friday after monitoring difficulties among candidates, including voting involving UAE's Lana Nusseibeh. The current term of Antonio Guterres ends Dec. 31.
items.title: Türkiye Nominates Sinirlioglu to Break UN Chief Deadlock

items.summary: A 21-year-old man, Amrit Sharma, was found hanging inside a rented house in Bihar's Begusarai district while his girlfriend Archana Kumari, aged 20, remained locked in another room. Police say the couple concealed their relationship by posing as siblings and submitting fake Aadhaar cards to the landlord around a month ago. Preliminary investigation points to suicide, though police said further inquiry would follow once the family files a formal complaint; Amrit's brother alleges threats from Archana's former boyfriend, which police have yet to connect to the death.
items.title: Bihar Man Found Hanging After Girlfriend Locked in Room Amid Alleged Sibling Ruse

items.summary: An anonymous donor pledged $225 million to Centre College in Kentucky, US, announced on October 16, 2026. The gift will establish the Centre Forever Fund to provide endowed merit-based and need-based scholarships. It anchors Pillars of Excellence: The Campaign for Centre College, a $450 million fundraising initiative launched alongside the pledge. Since its quiet phase began in 2020, supporters raised $350 million toward doubling an endowment valued at approximately $450 million. President Milton C. Moreland said the gift would support preparing students as community leaders; vice president Jess Metzmeier noted it would expand access and student success. The college has not announced how many students will receive scholarships or individual amounts.
items.title: Anonymous Donor Pledges $225 Million for Centre College Scholarships

items.summary: The Myhal Family Foundation has pledged C$10 million (£5.5 million) to support hospital redevelopment projects in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada. The gift will fund the Built for Us campaign and create a dollar-for-dollar matching challenge beginning on 29 October 2026, encouraging public contributions toward construction across Trillium Health Partners hospitals. Rayla Myhal made the donation with her husband George in memory of their late father Mehraj Din, who received care from the network. The funds will help build the new Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital and expand other facilities as part of what officials describe as Canada's largest hospital redevelopment project.
items.title: Canadian Foundation Donates C$10 Million for Mississauga Hospital Redevelopment

items.summary: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation is running its fifth Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign from November 1 to 30, encouraging pensioners under the Employees' Pension Scheme to submit annual life certificates digitally instead of visiting offices. Organised by the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare with technical support from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the Unique Identification Authority of India, the campaign covers around 2,000 cities and districts. Assistant Regional Commissioner Mithilesh Kumar Chaudhary said the Agra office would inform local pensioners about the facilities. The government has set a target of generating 2.30 crore digital life certificates, including 1.50 crore through face authentication on Android and iOS smartphones.
items.title: EPFO Launches Digital Life Certificate Campaign Across India

items.summary: Ahead of the November 3 US mid., surveys indicate Indian-Americans currently favour Democratic candidates, even as their party identification has declined. An AP-NORC/AAPI Data survey found only 25% of AAPI adults approved of Trump's performance, while a Carnegie Endowment poll showed 71% disapproval among Indian-Americans. HIT Strategies data put likely South Asian-American voters at 60% for Democrats in Congress, with 25% of former Trump backers shifting to the mid.. Concerns over immigration, rising living costs and US-India tensions shape these views, though party loyalty remains fluid rather than firmly Democratic.
items.title: Indian-American Voters Lean Democratic Amid Trump Disapproval Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: Three Kuki men were killed Saturday in a fresh exchange of gunfire between unidentified armed groups suspected to belong to the Naga and Kuki communities, marking the first fatal incident since October 29. The killing coincided with a large rally in Imphal demanding termination of the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement with Kuki-Zo armed groups and greater protection for local communities. Kuki Inpi Manipur accused the National Socialist Council of Nagaland-Isak Muivah and the Zeliangrong United Front-Kamson of responsibility, calling it a consequence of inadequate state security. Participants adopted resolutions demanding an end to what they described as a proxy war, replacement of Assam Rifles with a neutral force along the India-Myanmar border, implementation of the National Register of Citizens, and removal of deputy chief minister Nemcha Kipgen from the cabinet.
items.title: Kuki Activists Rally in Imphal Over SoO Pact and Community Security

items.summary: The Union government released an additional instalment of tax devolution totalling over Rs 1.09 lakh crore, with the finance ministry stating it disbursed Rs 1,09,019 crore to state governments on Saturday. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman attributed the second additional instalment this financial year to stronger economic activity and buoyant tax collections, noting it would help States accelerate infrastructure development and welfare spending ahead of the festive season.
items.title: Centre releases extra tax devolution to States

items.summary: Jatin Dev won the Boys Under-19 title at the 12th Late Samreddy Sudershan Reddy Memorial Telangana State Table Tennis Tournament in Hyderabad on Saturday. He beat Yashvasin 4-2 in the final with a verdict of 6-11, 11-8, 7-11, 13-11, 11-6, 11-8 at Mahaveer Institute of Science and Technology in Bandlaguda. The event was organised by the Ranga Reddy District Table Tennis Association.
items.title: Jatin Dev Wins Telangana Under-19 Table Tennis Title

items.summary: A Visual Capitalist ranking published in 2026 places doctors, scientists and teachers among the world's most trusted professions, with politicians, influencers and ministers near the bottom. The chart draws on the Ipsos Global Trustworthiness Index 2026, which surveyed 23,537 adults across 31 countries. Doctors led with a net trust score of 43 percentage points, followed by scientists at 42 and teachers at 37.
items.title: Visual Capitalist Ranks Doctors and Scientists as Most Trusted Professions in 2026

items.summary: A U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency report, Challenges to Security in Space, warns China could use directed-energy weapons in orbit by the end of the 2020s. Victoria Samson of the Secure World Foundation said she would be very surprised if China fielded space-based laser weapons by the late 2020s. The Global Times dismissed the report as alarmist and accused Washington of hyping threats while building its own orbit capabilities.
items.title: U.S. Intelligence Report Warns China May Deploy Space Laser Weapons by 2030

items.summary: The item is a short list titled Saturday assorted links, pairing brief notes on several topics. It points to the World Bank African urbanization report, suggesting that building out African cities well may define the coming era. It also mentions a summary of The Commanding Heights as one account of what is happening in Poland, while noting it does not endorse any particular interpretation.
items.title: Saturday assorted links roundup of urbanization and interpretation pieces

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Atlanta from October 30 to 31 for discussions on the Ukraine conflict, the Gulf situation and multilateral issues. The meeting occurred on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting hosted by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on October 30 and 31. Jaishankar confirmed the encounter via a photograph posted on X on Saturday, October 31, writing: 'Discussed the Ukraine conflict, Gulf situation and multilateral issues with FM Sergey Lavrov of Russia.' The talks also covered energy security, global supply chains, food security and shipping routes including the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea. Jaishankar separately called for diplomacy over military action at the gathering.
items.title: Jaishankar and Lavrov Meet in Atlanta on Ukraine, Gulf

items.summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the second additional instalment of tax devolution for the current financial year was supported by strong economic activity and buoyant tax collections. She added that the funds would help states accelerate infrastructure development, finance welfare programmes and support economic growth. Uttar Pradesh received the largest allocation at ₹19,208 crore, followed by Bihar (₹10,845 crore), Madhya Pradesh (₹8,010 crore), West Bengal (₹7,866 crore), Maharashtra (₹7,022 crore) and Rajasthan (₹6,460 crore). Odisha received ₹4,819 crore and Andhra Pradesh ₹4,597 crore.
items.title: Centre Releases Second Tax-Devolution Instalment to States

items.summary: After a security incident that led to the theft of crypto assets, Binance said ten major cryptocurrencies on its platform are fully backed at a minimum 1:1 ratio. The exchange said holders can verify holdings through its Proof of Reserves system once a fresh snapshot is generated. A complete zero-knowledge proof may take around 40-50 hours and could be available by November 3, Binance estimates.
items.title: Binance Offers Proof of Reserves After Crypto Theft

items.summary: In Bhopal, a payment dispute between survey agency Geolink Survey and government authorities has stalled complete handover of technical data for surveys of the Kerwa and Kaliasot reservoirs carried out to demarcate the Bhoj Wetland. The incomplete digital imagery and geo-referenced data have reportedly delayed encroachment assessment along both boundaries, which a National Green Tribunal committee had ordered.
items.title: Bhopal Reservoir Survey Data Handover Stalled Over Payment Dispute

items.summary: BJP leader Prasad, speaking at the Bihar BJP headquarters in Patna on Patel's 151st birth anniversary, criticized a Congress-led INDIA bloc 'public impeachment' of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as an empty mock parliament. He called Rahul Gandhi irresponsible and alleged Nehru became prime minister through vote chori, while claiming people would reject the Samajwadi Party in 2027 and Congress in 2029 polls.
items.title: BJP Leader Prasad Alleges Nehru Won PM Role Through Vote Theft

items.summary: In Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, an elderly man reportedly consumed a poisonous substance at the District Court premises on Saturday amid harassment over a financial dispute. Identified as Abdul Aziz of Fazalpura, he alleged that Sajid and Aslam harassed him for about a year while owing Rs 21,000, having deposited Rs 7,000 and paid another Rs 7,000 to Sajid. He claimed assaults, snatched Rs 300, and threats against his child. Police rushed him to Government Charak Hospital; he is being treated while officials await his statement.
items.title: Elderly Man Consumes Poison at Ujjain Court Over Money Dispute

items.summary:
The United Kingdom approved development of the Jackdaw North Sea gas field on October 21, ending years of legal challenges after a judge had rescinded environmental consent over carbon emissions. Owned by Adura, a Shell and Equinor joint venture since 2025, the field lies about 240 km east of Aberdeen. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said drilling would “protect hundreds of jobs,” though energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh admitted it will create just 27 jobs. The government plans an energy wealth fund with a £2 billion down payment to reinvest in climate transition, while critics including Tessa Khan and Zack Polanski called the move oversold and “climate vandalism.” Estimates of its contribution range from about 2 per cent to around 10 per cent at peak production.

visual:null
items.title: UK Approves Jackdaw Gas Field Amid Climate Debate

items.summary: In Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, the former Jones and Laughlin steel mill site Mill 19 has been repurposed into a hub for tech, robotics and advanced manufacturing. Photograph: Ross Mantle.
items.title: Mill 19 Becomes Creative Hub in Former Steel Factory

items.summary: Author Louise Kennedy explains how she became a writer after working as a chef for about 30 years and leaving her restaurant to study creative writing. Her first book, The End of the World Is a Cul de Sac, was published in 2021 when she was 55 and won the John McGahern Prize. In an interview with Scroll, Kennedy recounts that at 47 a friend persuaded her to join a writing group; after one night she felt unable to do anything else but write. She discusses Ireland's literary heritage, state support such as Aosdána funding of around €20,000 a year, and the themes in her novels Trespasses and Stations about language, identity and youth.
items.title: Louise Kennedy on Becoming an Author at Fifty-Five

items.summary: Passengers on some of Great Britain’s busiest railway lines have been warned of significant disruption from about ten days of engineering works over the festive period. Network Rail said most routes would stay open, as services generally stop on 25 and 26 December, making it the best time for essential work worth about £152m to improve reliability and capacity. Paddington station will close until January; Birmingham New Street closes five days from Christmas Eve to replace overhead power supplies; the east coast mainline is partly closed on Christmas Eve; TransPennine services between Leeds and Manchester are slowed for six weeks after Huddersfield’s closure.
items.title: Network Rail warns of Christmas engineering disruption across Britain

items.summary: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said Karnataka has identified 2,500 acres of alternative land, including forest land, to support the Mekedatu balancing reservoir across the Cauvery river. He added that once implemented, the project would let the state store 66 TMC of water and regulate releases downstream while it must release 177 TMC annually. Only around 500-odd acres of farmers' land is expected to be acquired.
items.title: Karnataka CM identifies land for Mekedatu project swap

items.summary: Biotech founder Gabriel Ocana Santero reported that an AI agent performed a brain injection on a live mouse. Working with his startup Exin Therapeutics in San Francisco, the team connected the model to surgical equipment and asked it to select one of 19 treatments for epilepsy gene therapy. A human surgeon first opened the skull while the agent observed; it then chose the treatment, region, coordinates, and injection parameters. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 refused to inject but agreed after switching to Claude Sonnet 5. The experiment lasted slightly longer than an hour versus a typical 45 minutes due to a coordinate glitch that the agent could not fix on its own. Santero says human oversight remains essential and it is far too soon for AI agents to work on human brains.
items.title: AI Agent Injected Drugs Into a Live Mouse's Brain, Biotech Founder Reports

items.summary: The INDIA bloc is staging a large protest and rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, opposing what it calls 'vote chori'—the alleged deletion of voters through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls—and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Opposition leaders are arriving from across states for a march named 'Chalo Dilli,' beginning at noon and culminating in an afternoon rally. The bloc's leaders say they expect up to 10 lakh people, while Delhi Police expects around 50,000; officials estimate the venue holds between 30,000 and 40,000 with arrangements in place. More than 4,000 police personnel are deployed for security across the route and grounds.
items.title: INDIA bloc gears up for mega rally at Ramlila Maidan over electoral roll concerns

items.summary: The ruling Aam Aadmi Party in Punjab released its first list of 40 candidates for the Assembly elections scheduled for February 2027. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann will contest from his Dhuri constituency, and state Industries Minister Sanjeev Arora was renominated from Ludhiana West despite an alleged money laundering case. Of the 40 candidates, five come from Majha, eight from Doaba, and 27 from Malwa region. The first list also includes four women candidates and seven Scheduled Caste members. Mann said selection would be based on performance and public surveys, reported The Indian Express.
items.title: AAP Names First Election Candidates Led by Mann From Dhuri

items.summary: Samajwadi Party leader and former Uttar Pradesh Cabinet minister Azam Khan was detained by the Enforcement Directorate minutes after being released on bail from Rampur jail. The ED is probing a money laundering case over Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, attaching assets valued at approximately Rs 1,170 crore while identifying alleged proceeds of crime worth Rs 426.46 crore under the PMLA. Khan's supporters called it 'the punishment for being a Muslim.'
items.title: ED Re-detains Azam Khan Minutes After Bail in Jauhar University Money Laundering Case

items.summary: Digvijay Nikam, a PhD student at JNU’s Centre for English Studies, reviews Amit Chaudhuri’s Château Rouge (169 pages), positioning it among rare Indian novels set in European cities that avoid the travelogue form. Drawing on Nirmal Verma’s Prague-set Ve Din (1964) as precedent, Nikam argues the unnamed protagonist dismantles idealised Paris rather than depicting an immigrant city or decolonising Europe; Chaudhuri states his objective was to access “the here and now.” The review notes the novel’s unconventional paragraph structure, its meditative tone, and its closing homage to Hemingway’s A Moveable Feast. Nikam concludes that Chaudhuri continues reshaping realist fiction.“Nothing is predictable in an Amit Chaudhuri novel,” he writes.
items.title: A Reviewer Frames Amit Chaudhuri’s Paris Novel as an Anti-Travelogue

items.summary: A TryHackMe article argues that bug bounties let learners test skills on real software, but recent program closures raise uncertainty about the path. It cites curl ending its paid bounty after submission quality fell from above 15% to below 5%, with Stenberg noting improvement back toward roughly 15-16%. The piece advises building foundations in HTTP and networking, using labs for safe practice, applying AI carefully, and writing fully reproducible reports before submitting. It frames readiness as dependent on skills and program rules rather than a fixed outcome, positioning TryHackMe's structured paths as support throughout learning.
items.title: TryHackMe Guides Beginners Through Verifiable Bug Bounty Skills

items.summary: Blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis disclosed a security incident after attackers used what it describes as offensive agentic techniques to access its internal systems earlier this month. Some customer information, including names and email addresses, was reached, but the company reports no evidence that investigation data or authentication credentials were exposed. It is still determining which records were accessed per organization.
items.title: Chainalysis Discloses Breach After Agentic-Style Attack

items.summary: A 21-year-old man, Hemanth alias Dummu, was arrested after allegedly attacking a Class 10 student with a chainsaw inside her classroom at Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu, Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh, on Saturday morning. The victim, Gopika, sustained severe injuries to her face, head, neck and back, and is being shifted to Bengaluru for advanced treatment after emergency surgery; a second student who tried to intervene was also injured but reported stable. Police are investigating an alleged harassment angle, citing the rejection of his proposal as a possible motive, though it has not been independently established. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu condemned the attack and monitored her recovery.
items.title: Andhra Man Arrested After Chainsaw Attack on Schoolgirl

items.summary: Kyoto-based Doshisha's chairman Eiji Hatta apologized at his first press conference since the March 16 accident that killed one female student, Tomoka Takeishi. He cited education ministry findings of serious safety-management failures and resigned to implement governance improvements.
items.title: Doshisha Chairman Apologizes Over Fatal Okinawa Boat Accident and Resigns

items.summary: The United States, South Korea and Japan restated their commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea at a Group of 20 meeting in Atlanta. Pyongyang rejected disarmament while speculation grows over possible Trump–Kim talks next month.
items.title: Three allies reaffirm North Korea denuclearization pledge

items.summary: Two blockchain analytics firms, TRM Labs and Chainalysis, say they hold robust intelligence identifying the Lazarus Group as a likely culprit in the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. The attribution is described with high confidence by both groups but remains an accusation; Binance has not directly commented on potential North Korean links and initially blamed a compromised engineer's laptop before acknowledging a wider breach.
items.title: Blockchain firms point North Korean hackers at Binance breach

items.summary: Multiple drone strikes hit northern Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians including children and pregnant women, witnesses told AFP on Friday. In Amhara, a witness said four strikes struck a displaced-person camp just as students returned from school; others reported 14 and 15 deaths there. A Tigray strike killed at least 11 people hit by a second blast while collecting grain in Rama town. ACLED attributed the attack to the ENDF and cited 12 civilian deaths. The Ethiopian army declined comment, amid fears of wider conflict near Eritrea's border.
items.title: Drone Strikes in Ethiopia Kill at Least 25 Civilians

items.summary: British punk critic Jon Savage discusses his 2024 book The Secret Public: How LGBTQ Resistance Shaped Popular Culture (1955-1979), published by EL PAÍS. He explains that covering a queer subtext in music was difficult to establish in the 1950s, and describes how he connected dots through friends who listened to Motown and Dusty Springfield. Savage notes that backlash against LGBTQ+ gains has intensified over the last 20 years, and says his book ends in 1979 at the National March on Washington for Lesbian and Gay Rights because he did not want to write about AIDS.
items.title: Jon Savage on Queer Music and His New Book

items.summary: A government survey showed China's official manufacturing purchasing managers' index fell to 49.3 from 50.1 in September, its third contraction in four months, according to the National Bureau of Statistics on Saturday (Oct 31). The reading missed a forecast for 50.0 from a Reuters poll and was weighed down by soft export demand and weak domestic consumer spending after the National Day holiday. Analyst Zhang Liqun of the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing said insufficient demand is increasing downward pressure on the economy, urging policymakers to act soon.
items.title: China's factory output shrank for a third straight month in October

items.summary: Eight years ago, Otter.ai launched a free real-time transcription app. In 2026 it is competing against many AI transcription rivals and now aims to extract insights from captured conversations rather than just transcribe them. New CMO Alex Gay says meetings are often inefficient because participants arrive unprepared or follow-ups slip away, creating what she calls “this loop of having to have more meetings.” Otter introduced three new features Tuesday built around the whole meeting life cycle and rewards organization-wide use across its free Basic tier plus Pro ($99.96), Business ($239.88 per user per year) and Enterprise tiers.
items.title: Otter.ai Expands Beyond Transcription Into Meeting Intelligence

items.summary: The article asks what corporate AI needs next, comparing it to the moment PageRank changed search in 1998. It argues companies require persistent memory, state and learning loops rather than just answers, built on older tools like Python that agents are escaping. The author claims competition is shifting from model capabilities toward system performance, citing researchers at Berkeley's AI research blog who describe a move to compound systems.
items.title: Corporate AI's PageRank Moment Shifts Focus From Models To Systems

items.summary: Parameter Labs describes an exploit against ChatGPT's artifacts pattern, formerly called Canvas and now HTML previews. The vulnerability lets untrusted code in a sandboxed iframe inject custom HTML via innerHTML, bypassing CSP rules through YouTube oEmbed to execute JavaScript. This enables fetching private user data from APIs and exfiltrating it via image references. A malicious share URL could let another signed-in user access their data or take actions on their behalf. OpenAI closed the hole and paid a $5,000 bug bounty.
items.title: Parameter Labs Exploits ChatGPT Account Takeover Vulnerability

items.summary: A US appeals court upheld the dismissal of a Canadian publisher's lawsuit against Meta over its 2020 shutdown of the company's Facebook pages. In October 2026, the Ninth Circuit ruled that Section 230 protected Meta because removing content is part of its editorial role as a publisher. Shared Partnership had argued losing access to roughly 25 million followers harmed its business built on advertising and provocative clickbait campaigns. The court rejected both conversion and breach-of-contract arguments, affirming the lower court's decision that Section 230 shields platforms from liability for content decisions.
items.title: Ninth Circuit upholds dismissal of Shared Partnership's conversion claim against Meta

items.summary: Delhi is preparing for the INDIA bloc's anti-CEC rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, preceded by a 'Chalo Dilli' march from Minto Road-Connaught Place junction. Opposition parties project a turnout of up to 10 lakh people, while Delhi Police expects around 50,000 and deploys more than 4,000 personnel plus 200 CCTV cameras. The rally follows a symbolic 'public impeachment' resolution moved by the bloc against former Speaker Meira Kumar.
items.title: Delhi Prepares for INDIA Bloc Anti-CEC Rally at Ramlila Maidan

items.summary: Fitch Ratings placed France's credit score on a negative outlook in an unscheduled move, citing weaker growth, higher borrowing costs and a wider deficit. The country stays at A+, but bond spreads rose to 178 basis points over Germany. Finance Minister Roland Lescure urged passage of a responsible budget before year-end as political gridlock persists.
items.title: Fitch Puts France on Negative Outlook Amid Fiscal Concerns

items.summary: Ruchira Ranasingha, a 50-year-old Sri Lankan woman, has been stranded on the Cook Islands for three years after being unable to obtain transit visas. She left Sri Lanka in 2018 and sought asylum in New Zealand before following an adviser's recommendation to exit temporarily to apply for a work visa overseas. After leaving New Zealand, she breached her asylum-linked visa terms, prompting rejections of multiple transit applications from both New Zealand and Australia. Other destinations require biometric processing only available in New Zealand. Ranasingha says the immigration firm gave her "terrible advice"; Immigration New Zealand declined visas citing no genuine intention to transit. Her family and Sri Lanka's foreign ministry are seeking help as she faces mounting health stress, saying she would go home even handcuffed.
items.title: Woman Stranded in Cook Islands After Failed Transit Visas

items.summary: Poland's prime minister Donald Tusk vowed to complete a contested overhaul of the constitutional court, telling viewers "in certain matters, there can be no compromise". He defended suspending PiS-appointed judges after they seized control and accused opposition figures of seeking to destroy democracy. The move sets up next year's election amid divided experts on its legality.
items.title: Tusk Defends Constitutional Court Overhaul Amid Protests

items.summary: Saul Canelo Alvarez reclaimed his world super middleweight title with a unanimous decision over Christian Mbilli in Riyadh on Saturday. The judges scored the fight 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110. Alvarez landed cleaner blows than the French champion to re-establish himself among boxing's elite after his first ring return in more than a year. Canelo said he still loves the sport.
items.title: Canelo Alvarez Reclaims Super Middleweight Title Over Mbilli

items.summary: Walking into Saki, a Japanese kappō-style restaurant serving omakase on the 29th floor of the JW Marriott Tokyo, visitors see views of Rainbow Bridge and Odaiba. First opened in October 2025 alongside the hotel, it is led by Emmanuel Stroobant of Saint Pierre and Kazumine Nishida of Shoukouwa, both two-Michelin-starred establishments in Singapore.
items.title: Saki debuts omakase dining atop JW Marriott Tokyo

items.summary: Golden Gai, a small cluster of bars in Shinjuku’s Kabukicho district that now draws tourists but was once hard for outsiders to enter, is the subject of ‘Moonlit Golden-Gai.’ The film marks the feature debut of 63-year-old television veteran Shinji Nishiki. It offers an inside look at one bar based on a real establishment he himself once visited.
items.title: Shinji Nishiki debuts Moonlit Golden-Gai on Shinjuku bars

items.summary: The Vietnamese government announced on Saturday that it will lower its average retail electricity price by 2 per cent and eliminate the special consumption tax on gasoline from November 1. The moves aim to support economic stability, social welfare and business activity while reducing costs for households and businesses.
items.title: Vietnam Cuts Electricity Prices and Gasoline Tax From November

items.summary: Robert Yeomans and Heidy Perez Perez share how the loss of their unborn son Thiago shaped them in unexpected ways. They met on a language-learning app while living in Adelaide, reconnecting about a year later before building a life together in Australia. Pregnant with Thiago shortly after their 2021 wedding, they were told at 28 weeks that he was not growing properly and had placental issues; Heidy gave birth to him by C-section the same day she lost his heartbeat on their anniversary. They describe grieving differently while holding onto each other, learning patience, compassion and what it means to love someone through pain.
items.title: A couple on grief and love after losing their baby

items.summary: Hunter Valley wineries increasingly source grapes from the cool-climate Orange wine region in Central West NSW as climate change makes lighter-style wines harder to produce locally. Winemaker Ross McDonald of Macquariedale Organic Wines, who moved there in 2020, says conditions suit shiraz and cabernet ripening. Industry bodies note fruit is purchased for supply consistency amid weather variability. Wine Australia's National Vintage Report showed Orange crushed almost five times as much pinot noir as the Hunter Valley this year: 343 tonnes worth about $730,000 versus 69 tonnes worth about $71,000.
items.title: Climate and taste shifts drive Orange wine region growth

items.summary: Crypto exchange Binance said on Saturday it has replaced 90 per cent of assets stolen in a record US$6.3 billion hack, using company funds to buy new tokens and committing to cover the remaining 10 per cent so users bear no financial impact. Co-CEO Richard Teng stated customers' funds were safe. The FBI blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor unit for converting stolen assets into ethereum. Binance set aside around US$6.34 billion from its Secure Asset Fund, Futures Insurance Fund and corporate treasury, and plans to reopen withdrawals on Sunday as it runs a proof-of-reserves process covering 10 listed tokens at a minimum 1:1 ratio.
items.title: Binance Covers Most Losses From Record Hack

items.summary: Honorata Jamrozik, a Dartford mother of two who won £1 million in the Omaze Monthly Millionaire Draw in 2026, gave £5,000 to her neighbours after 14 years together so their family could take its first holiday abroad. She described them as family and said she regarded them that way since they moved in. Jamrozik had spent 7 years fostering before stepping away to care for elderly parents in Poland, where the win may let her return. The Good News Network reported the gift came two weeks after her father's funeral; she viewed it as a blessing from him. Her husband, unaware of their Omaze subscription, joked about winning millions. Jamrozik and her husband plan an anniversary trip to Poland in October 2026.
items.title: Lottery Winner Funds Neighbours' First Overseas Holiday

items.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's film 'Ramayana' stars Sai Pallavi as a warrior princess skilled in sword fighting and martial arts, departing from the traditional image of grace, devotion and sacrifice. This portrayal prompts reflection on whether Sita has always been seen only as someone needing rescue or carries a more powerful legacy.
items.title: Sai Pallavi's Ramayana Sita Revives Warrior Legacy Debate

items.summary: Chevron is raising its exploration budget this year by 50% compared with last year, McLachlan told the Financial Times in an interview in September. The company says spending could top $1. 5 billion, up from just below $1 billion in 2025. Kevin McLachlan leads Chevron’s revived upstream program and took over the exploration arm last year after joining from France’s TotalEnergies. Two years ago Chevron drilled about 10 exploration wells per year; its 2027 plan includes drilling 20 exploration wells, possibly up to six appraisal wells. About half of the budget is now going into undeveloped frontier basins in South America, Africa and the Eastern Mediterranean, up from around 20% a few years ago. Chevron also raised acreage by 35% over the past year and has announced discoveries in Nigeria and Angola. Analysts at Wood Mackenzie said the Middle East conflict highlighted concentration risk in unstable regions.
items.title: Chevron Boosts Exploration Spending by Half

items.summary: St Pious won the third season of the Crimson International Basketball Championship, defeating Army Public School 54-42 at St Michael's High School premises in Alwal. The team led 23-16 at half-time and held advantage across all four quarters with better scoring consistency. Officials described an impressive all-round performance from both sides.
items.title: St Pious Basketball Champions of Crimson International Tournament

items.summary: The Bhopal district administration began relocating nearly half-century-old sawmill units obstructing the Bhopal Metro rail alignment. Around 108 sawmills are scheduled to be shifted, with about 40 slated for Chhota Ratibad and others accommodated at an 18-acre site in Palwaliya Road area. On the first day, around 10 sawmills near Pul Patra were removed. The administration sealed nine additional sawmills at Bharat Talkies Timber Market area over alleged government-land occupation following a Tehsildar eviction order. Some operators initially protested; officials said notices had been served and deadlines expired.
items.title: Bhopal Administration Relocates and Seals Sawmills Along Metro Route

items.summary: In an Agrispective Podcast episode, host Subramani Ra Mancombu speaks with Mangesh Wange, CEO of Swades Foundation, about how El Niño-driven weather disruptions and climate change affect India's farming sector. The discussion covers rainfall deficits, drought-like conditions, water scarcity and crop losses in rural Maharashtra, then turns to adaptation strategies such as large-scale irrigation projects, farm ponds, crop diversification and integrated livelihood models to help farmers reduce risk amid erratic monsoons.
items.title: Podcast Explores El Niño and Climate Change for Indian Farmers

items.summary: The Indore Municipal Corporation added a 'Know Your Safai Mitra' feature to the Indore 311 app, letting residents identify sanitation workers in their area and submit feedback. Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargav and municipal commissioner Kshitij Singhal launched it Saturday; additional commissioner Prakhar Singh said users can check whether a worker is on duty, on leave or absent. Officials expect it to improve transparency and accountability.
items.title: Indore launches worker-tracking module on civic app

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), met Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee in Delhi on Saturday. He thanked her for supporting the outfit's youth-led protests and standing with members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka during their arrest by Delhi Police. Although the CJP expressed solidarity with Sunday's INDIA bloc rally against alleged 'vote chori', Dipke clarified that the party would not formally join, citing its independent and politically neutral identity. Banerjee praised the activists as movement pioneers and invited them to West Bengal.
items.title: CJP Founder Rejects INDIA Bloc Rally Despite Meeting Banerjee
